meta.spec_reference: ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015 (ISO Base Media File Format, 5th edition) for the box grammar, sample tables and movie fragments; ISO/IEC 14496-14 (MP4 file format) for brands; ISO/IEC 14496-15 for the AVC sample entry and AVCDecoderConfigurationRecord; ISO/IEC 23001-7 (Common Encryption) for pssh, tenc, senc, saiz and saio; Apple QuickTime File Format (2016) for the mvhd/tkhd/mdhd/vmhd/hdlr layouts and the language and graphics-mode enumerations the template uses

schema_extensions.name: applies_when
schema_extensions.where: most constraints entries keyed on the mp4box struct
schema_extensions.why: The template puts every box body in one switch inside a single struct (lines 469-801), so field names collide across box types by design -- version, flag, entry_count, sample_count, duration, reserved and entries are each declared in many cases. The constraints map is keyed by struct.field, so one key legitimately covers several box types and this field says which, and where the meaning differs.

schema_extensions.name: per_box_semantics
schema_extensions.where: constraints entries whose meaning genuinely differs between box types (mp4box.entry_count, mp4box.sample_count, mp4box.sample_size, mp4box.entries, mp4box.flag, mp4box.duration, mp4box.reserved)
schema_extensions.why: applies_when says which boxes a key covers; this says what the field means and what it is computed from in each of them, because a single algorithm string cannot describe stsd, stts, stco and saio at once.

schema_extensions.name: nested_wrapper_convention
schema_extensions.where: meta, and implicitly every field of a single-member wrapper struct
schema_extensions.why: fp16, fp32, fp32uvw, fourcc, mp4time, mp4lang and compatible_brand each wrap exactly one scalar. Instances of them carry no storage of their own and are constrained at their leaf. The complete list of such instances, all deliberately covered at the leaf rather than omitted, is: mp4box.hdr (464), mp4box.box (447, 488, 806), matrix.a through matrix.w as fp32/fp32uvw instances, mp4box.create_time (743, 753, 778), mp4box.modify_time (744, 754, 779), mp4box.language (747), mp4box.preferred_rate (757), mp4box.preferred_volume (758), mp4box.matrix_structure (760, 788), mp4box.balance (772), mp4box.volume (786), mp4box.opcolor (796), mp4box.brand (726), and mp4box.references (642), which is an array of str_sidx records whose fields carry their own entries and whose element count is constrained under mp4box.reference_count. Instances that DO carry a constraint distinct from their leaf -- boxheader.type, mp4box.major_brand, mp4box.type, mp4box.subtype, mp4box.width, mp4box.height -- have their own entries.

schema_extensions.name: unnamed_payloads
schema_extensions.why: The single largest payload in an MP4, the mdat media data, has NO field name in this template: mdat is absent from the switch at lines 469-801 and is consumed by FSkip(contentsize) at line 799. A hard rule forbids inventing a key for it, but the rewrite step still needs to know what belongs inside it, so its requirement is recorded here instead of in constraints.

schema_extensions.name: measured_gate
schema_extensions.where: constraints.mp4box.entries, constraints.mp4box.entry_count, constraints.mp4box.chunk_offset, constraints.mp4box.entry_size, constraints.boxheader.size, and meta.unnamed_payloads
schema_extensions.why: The decoder_gate claims for this format were measured rather than assumed: a minimal MP4 was hand-built from the generation_strategy below and each field was then corrupted in isolation and fed to ffprobe and ffmpeg. This key records the exact observed behaviour and the exact diagnostic text, because several widely believed gates turned out not to be gates at all.

schema_extensions.name: excluded_values
schema_extensions.why: Box sizes 2 through 7 are smaller than the box header itself and make the template's contentsize computation at line 467 underflow an unsigned 64-bit value. This names those six values without bounding the field: 0, 1 and everything from 8 upward stay free.

schema_extensions.name: template_parse_requirement
schema_extensions.why: Box size 0 means 'extends to end of file' in ISO/IEC 14496-12 and was measured to work correctly in ffmpeg, but the template's BoxSize helper at line 172 returns 0 for it so endOffset collapses onto startOffset. The distinction between a format rule and a template limitation matters to the rewrite step and has no other home.

schema_extensions.name: declared_but_unreferenced
schema_extensions.why: str_stsd is defined at lines 440-449 but the line that would instantiate it, line 666, is commented out in favour of line 667. The fields are real .bt fields and are recorded, but the generator must know they are dead unless the stsd case is changed back.

schema_extensions.name: context_value_sets
schema_extensions.why: fourcc is instantiated for three unrelated purposes -- box types, file-type brands and handler types -- with three disjoint legal sets. One valid_values array cannot express that without implying a brand is a legal box type, so the sets are carried separately by instantiation site.

schema_extensions.name: tier
schema_extensions.why: must_remain_unconstrained means different things for a Tier C axis (emit the whole declared field width), a Tier B axis (emit every legal value) and the Tier A axes listed (the value is fixed by an identity, but the free quantity it records must not be pinned).

schema_extensions.name: no_fixed_value_note
schema_extensions.why: Checklist item 1 requires a re-scan for magic numbers, markers, terminators and separators. MP4 has none of them as named fields, and a silent absence would look like an omission rather than a finding, so the reason is stated explicitly.

meta.structure_note: MP4 is a flat recursive sequence of boxes, each a 32-bit size and a four-character type optionally followed by a 64-bit size, in which moov/trak/mdia/minf/stbl nest down to the sample tables that index the media bytes lying in a separate mdat box; the container itself carries no compressed payload the parser inspects -- mdat is skipped wholesale by this template at line 799 and by a demuxer alike -- and the one genuine payload_wellformedness requirement is the stsd sample entry at line 667, whose fixed 78-byte VisualSampleEntry prefix and nested codec configuration box were measured to be the difference between ffmpeg creating a decodable stream and creating no stream at all.
meta.no_fixed_value_note: Checklist item 1 asks that every magic number, signature, section marker, block terminator and field separator appear as a Tier A fixed_value. After a deliberate re-scan this file contains NONE, because MP4 has none. The format has no file magic: the template's own header at line 10 names 'ftyp' at offset 4 as its identifying bytes, but that is a box TYPE, one value of an open four-character enumeration, and ffmpeg was measured to demux a working file with the entire ftyp box removed. There are no terminators -- every box is delimited by its own length, and the top-level loop at line 804 ends on end of file rather than on a marker. There are no separators, because boxes are packed with no padding. The only genuinely fixed bytes in the format -- the AVC configuration record's configurationVersion of 1, and the six zero reserved bytes at the head of every sample entry -- lie INSIDE the stsd payload, which the template gives no field of its own, so they are recorded in constraints.mp4box.entries.must_produce rather than as fixed_value entries. Every length field is a calculated_value and every identifier is an enumerated_values; that is the honest shape of this format.

unnamed_payloads.where: reached through the default arm of the switch at line 798 and consumed by FSkip(contentsize) at line 799; the template gives it no field, so it cannot appear in constraints
unnamed_payloads.codec: codec-dependent; for the avc1 sample entry, AVC access units in AVCC length-prefixed form (ISO/IEC 14496-15)
unnamed_payloads.must_produce: for each sample, a run of (length, NAL unit) pairs where the length field is lengthSizeMinusOne+1 bytes big-endian, taken from the avcC record, and the lengths sum exactly to that sample's stsz entry_size; the bytes of each NAL unit are otherwise free
unnamed_payloads.decoder_gate: MEASURED: with the sample tables correct but the mdat bytes randomised, ffmpeg still creates the h264 stream but the decoder reports 'Invalid NAL unit size (-718053481 > 1323)' and produces zero frames; the same message appears when stco points anywhere other than the true start of the sample run. The demuxer is unaffected either way -- mdat is opaque to it.
unnamed_payloads.generation_strategy: Choose the sample sizes freely. For each sample write a 4-byte big-endian length L followed by L free bytes whose first byte has its high bit clear (a valid NAL header); repeat until the sample's declared entry_size is consumed exactly. Then set the stco chunk_offset to the absolute file offset at which the first sample begins. Nothing inside a NAL is checked by the demuxer, and only the length framing is checked by the decoder before it attempts to parse the slice.

meta.measured_gate_summary: A minimal MP4 was hand-built from the constructions recorded in this file and verified: ffprobe reported the h264 stream and ffmpeg decoded every frame with no error, at declared track dimensions of 1x1, 7x13, 64x48 and 1920x1080 and at timescales of 1, 5, 1000 and 90000, with no dimension ever adjusted to suit the payload. Each field was then corrupted in isolation. Producing NO STREAM AT ALL: a stsd entry_count that disagrees with the entries present ('invalid size 5 in stsd'), a sample entry whose declared size is 0 ('invalid size 0 in stsd'), and a sample entry truncated so its configuration box falls outside it. Producing a stream but ZERO FRAMES: a randomised avcC body ('No start code is found'), a wrong stco offset, all-zero stsz sizes, an stts entry_count of 0 ('missing mandatory atoms'), corrupted sample-entry reserved bytes ('Picture size 0x0'), and randomised mdat bytes. NOT gates in ffmpeg at all, contrary to expectation: a missing ftyp box, a box size field of 0, and a box size field of 3.

fp16.value.tier_rationale: This is the raw storage of every 8.8 fixed-point quantity in the format -- track volume, movie preferred volume, audio balance -- none of which any demuxer validates, so pinning it would make every file carry the same volume while reaching no new line.
fp16.value.description: The 16-bit signed backing value of an 8.8 fixed-point number, read as value/256.
fp16.value.notes: Instantiated as mp4box.preferred_volume (line 758), mp4box.balance (line 772) and mp4box.volume (line 786). The conventional full-scale value is 0x0100 and silence is 0, but negative values and values above full scale are representable, accepted and worth emitting because they reach the clamping code in any player that applies the gain.

fp32.value.tier_rationale: This backs every 16.16 fixed-point quantity -- the movie preferred rate, the edit list media rate, the track width and height and six of the nine matrix cells -- and a demuxer stores them without validation, so constraining it would flatten all of those at once.
fp32.value.description: The 32-bit signed backing value of a 16.16 fixed-point number, read as value/65536.
fp32.value.notes: Instantiated as mp4box.preferred_rate (757), mp4box.width (789), mp4box.height (790), elst_entry.media_rate (406) and matrix.a/b/c/d/x/y (354-361). Zero is meaningful and must stay reachable: a preferred_rate of 0 means paused and a media_rate of 0 is a dwell edit, both of which are separate paths. Negative values give mirrored matrices and reversed playback, which players handle in dedicated code.

fp32uvw.value.tier_rationale: This backs the three 2.30 fixed-point cells of the transformation matrix, which a player reads to decide display rotation; no value makes a demuxer refuse the file, and pinning it to the unity constant would delete every rotated and skewed presentation path.
fp32uvw.value.description: The 32-bit signed backing value of a 2.30 fixed-point number, read as value/0x40000000; used only for the u, v and w column of the matrix.
fp32uvw.value.notes: Instantiated as matrix.u (356), matrix.v (359) and matrix.w (362). The unity matrix uses 0, 0 and 0x40000000 for these three; ffmpeg reads the whole matrix into a display matrix side-data and derives a rotation angle from it, so non-unity values reach the rotation and transposition code that unity never does.

matrix.a.tier_rationale: Cell a of the presentation matrix, which together with b, c and d decides the rotation and scale a player applies; ffmpeg turns these into display-matrix side data, so pinning them to the unity constant would leave every rotation and flip path unreached.
matrix.a.description: The a cell of the 3x3 transformation matrix, a 16.16 fixed-point value; 0x00010000 in the unity matrix.
matrix.a.notes: The nine cells are stored in the order a b u c d v x y w (lines 354-362), which is the ISO and QuickTime row order; a, b, c, d, x and y are 16.16 while u, v and w are 2.30. The common non-unity values are the four 90-degree rotations, which set a and d to 0 and b and c to plus or minus 0x00010000; those are the ones that reach ffmpeg's rotation handling.

matrix.b.tier_rationale: Cell b of the presentation matrix; unvalidated by any demuxer, and non-zero values are precisely what trigger the rotation path.
matrix.b.description: The b cell of the transformation matrix, a 16.16 fixed-point value; 0 in the unity matrix.

matrix.u.tier_rationale: Cell u of the presentation matrix, in the 2.30 scale; unvalidated, and non-zero values give a perspective transform that only dedicated code handles.
matrix.u.description: The u cell of the transformation matrix, a 2.30 fixed-point value; 0 in the unity matrix.

matrix.c.tier_rationale: Cell c of the presentation matrix; unvalidated, and non-zero values are half of what makes a 90-degree rotation.
matrix.c.description: The c cell of the transformation matrix, a 16.16 fixed-point value; 0 in the unity matrix.

matrix.d.tier_rationale: Cell d of the presentation matrix; unvalidated, and a negative value gives a vertical flip that players handle separately.
matrix.d.description: The d cell of the transformation matrix, a 16.16 fixed-point value; 0x00010000 in the unity matrix.

matrix.v.tier_rationale: Cell v of the presentation matrix, in the 2.30 scale; unvalidated and free.
matrix.v.description: The v cell of the transformation matrix, a 2.30 fixed-point value; 0 in the unity matrix.

matrix.x.tier_rationale: The horizontal translation cell; unvalidated, and non-zero values offset the presentation in a way only the translation path handles.
matrix.x.description: The x translation cell of the transformation matrix, a 16.16 fixed-point value; 0 in the unity matrix.

matrix.y.tier_rationale: The vertical translation cell; unvalidated and free.
matrix.y.description: The y translation cell of the transformation matrix, a 16.16 fixed-point value; 0 in the unity matrix.

matrix.w.tier_rationale: The w cell of the presentation matrix, in the 2.30 scale; unvalidated, and a value other than 0x40000000 scales the whole transform in code nothing else reaches.
matrix.w.description: The w cell of the transformation matrix, a 2.30 fixed-point value; 0x40000000 in the unity matrix.

fourcc.value.tier_rationale: A four-character code the parser does not recognise makes it skip the box or ignore the identifier rather than refuse the file -- the template's own default arm at line 798 does exactly that -- so it is not a front gate; but the codes are registered enumerations and each recognised one selects a different parsing branch.
fourcc.value.description: The four-byte identifier backing every box type, file-type brand and handler type in the format.
fourcc.value.completeness_reason: The field is four free bytes and the ISO registration authority lists hundreds of box types with more added by each amendment, so no list can be closed. Those above are the box types the template names in its switch and its BoxComment function plus the ones a real demuxer branches on. Unregistered four-character codes remain legal and must also be generated, because an unknown box type is the only route into the FSkip(contentsize) skip path at line 799 and into a demuxer's equivalent.

context_value_sets.box_type: the valid_values list above; this is the set compared by the switch at line 469 and by BoxComment at line 203

fourcc.value.notes: The three context sets are disjoint in practice: 'vide' is a legal handler type but not a legal box type, and 'isom' is a legal brand but not a box type. A generator must pick from the set belonging to the instantiation site -- boxheader.type, mp4box.major_brand and compatible_brand.brand for the first two, mp4box.type and mp4box.subtype for the third. value_names is null because a four-character code is its own name.

boxheader.size.tier_rationale: This is the stride to the next box and the bound of the container walk at line 486; a value that disagrees with the bytes actually written leaves the parser inside the previous box, so every box after it is read from the wrong offset and the whole moov hierarchy is lost.
boxheader.size.description: Total size of this box in bytes, counting the size and type fields themselves and, when present, the 64-bit extended size.
boxheader.size.algorithm: total byte count of the box: 8 for the header, plus 8 more when size == 1 and a 64-bit size follows, plus the body; the special value 1 means the real size is in size64 and the special value 0 means the box runs to end of file
boxheader.size.covers: every byte of this box from the first byte of this field to the last byte of its body, including all nested boxes
boxheader.size.size_identity: the template computes contentsize = BoxSize(hdr) - sizeof(hdr) at line 467 via the helper at line 167, and endOffset = startOffset + BoxSize(hdr) at line 466; sizeof(hdr) is 8 normally and 16 when size == 1
boxheader.size.template_parse_requirement: Size 0, meaning the box extends to end of file, is legal ISO and was MEASURED to work correctly in ffmpeg, but the template's BoxSize helper at line 172 returns 0 for it, so endOffset collapses onto startOffset and a container box with size 0 parses none of its children. A generator targeting this template should write real sizes; a generator targeting a real demuxer may use 0 on the last box.
boxheader.size.measured_gate: MEASURED: a box size field of 0 and a box size field of 3 were both written onto the mdat box of a working file and ffmpeg decoded every frame unchanged in both cases -- neither is a gate in ffmpeg, though 2 through 7 make this template's unsigned contentsize underflow to an enormous value.
boxheader.size.notes: Never give this field an evil value. The excluded set is exactly the six values smaller than the 8-byte header, which no box can legitimately declare. 0, 1 and everything from 8 upward stay free, and large sizes are bounded by the output_budget on the box sequence, never by capping this field.

boxheader.type.tier_rationale: An unrecognised box type is skipped rather than refused -- the template's default arm at line 798 calls FSkip(contentsize) and a demuxer does the same -- so it is not a front gate; but it is the field the entire switch at line 469 dispatches on, and every registered type it is given is a parsing branch that would otherwise never run.
boxheader.type.description: The four-character type of this box, which selects how its body is parsed.
boxheader.type.completeness_reason: The type is four free bytes and the registry is open-ended. The list above is every type the template's switch at lines 469-801 and its BoxComment function at lines 203-245 name, plus the sample-entry and configuration types a demuxer needs. Unregistered types are legal, are skipped, and must be generated too -- the skip path is real code.
boxheader.type.notes: The thirteen container types listed in the switch at lines 472-484 -- dinf, edts, mdia, minf, moov, moof, stbl, trak, udta, traf, mvex, sinf, schi -- are the only ones whose bodies are walked as further boxes; every other named type is parsed field by field and everything else is skipped. Note that mdat, the largest box in a real file, is NOT in the switch and falls to the default skip at line 799.

boxheader.size64.tier_rationale: When size is 1 this field carries the real box length, so exactly the same consequence applies as for size: a wrong value leaves the parser inside the box and every following box is misread.
boxheader.size64.description: The 64-bit extended box size, present only when the 32-bit size field holds the escape value 1.
boxheader.size64.algorithm: total byte count of the box including the 8-byte header and these 8 bytes; the same quantity size would hold if it fitted
boxheader.size64.covers: every byte of this box from the first byte of boxheader.size to the last byte of its body
boxheader.size64.size_identity: size64 >= 16, since the header it measures is itself 16 bytes when this field is present
boxheader.size64.notes: Present if and only if size == 1, which the template tests at line 374. The 64-bit form exists for mdat boxes above 4 GiB; emitting it on a small box is legal, is handled by every demuxer, and is the only way to exercise the extended-header path, so a generator should use it occasionally regardless of the box's actual size rather than only when forced.

compatible_brand.brand.tier_rationale: A brand a reader does not recognise is ignored rather than refused, and ffmpeg was MEASURED to demux correctly with the entire ftyp box removed, so this is not a front gate; but the brands are a registered enumeration and each one a reader recognises unlocks a different set of structural expectations.
compatible_brand.brand.description: One entry of the ftyp box's compatible-brands list, declaring a specification the file conforms to.
compatible_brand.brand.completeness_reason: Brands are registered continuously and the field is four free bytes, so the list cannot be closed; these are the brands real readers branch on. Unregistered brands are legal and are ignored, which is itself the path a generator should reach.
compatible_brand.brand.notes: The number of compatible brands is free: the template's loop at line 724 runs until the box's content is consumed, so the count follows from the ftyp box size rather than from any count field. 'qt  ' and 'M4A ' have trailing spaces that are part of the four bytes, and 'dash' switches a reader into fragmented-file expectations, which is a large separate body of code.

mp4time.value.tier_rationale: Every creation and modification timestamp in the format is backed by this field; the prompt names timestamps as Tier C outright, no reader refuses any value, and the template's own display function at line 270 simply subtracts an epoch offset.
mp4time.value.description: A 32-bit timestamp in seconds since midnight on 1 January 1904, the classic Mac OS epoch.
mp4time.value.notes: Instantiated as mp4box.create_time (743, 753, 778) and mp4box.modify_time (744, 754, 779). Values below 2082844800 convert to dates before the POSIX epoch and make the template's quad arithmetic at line 270 go negative, which is a formatting path a modern timestamp never reaches; 0 is the epoch itself and is extremely common in real files. Nothing here is excluded.

mp4lang.value.tier_rationale: A language code a reader does not recognise is stored and ignored rather than refused, so it is not a front gate; but the field has two disjoint encodings and the template's ReadLang at line 276 branches between them, so which encoding is used selects a different interpretation path.
mp4lang.value.description: A media language, encoded either as a QuickTime language index below 0x0400 or as three packed 5-bit ISO 639-2 letters with the high bit clear.
mp4lang.value.completeness_reason: The QuickTime half is exhaustive -- every enumerator of the qtlang enum at lines 40-148 is listed, with the duplicate-valued pairs (Lettish/Latvian at 28, Saami/Sami at 29, Galla/Oromo at 87) collapsed onto their shared value. The ISO 639-2 half cannot be enumerated: any three lowercase letters pack into a distinct 16-bit value, giving thousands of legal codes, so only a few representative packings are listed and the packing rule is given in notes.
mp4lang.value.notes: The packing for the ISO half, taken from the template's ReadLang at lines 282-284, is value = ((c0-0x60) << 10) | ((c1-0x60) << 5) | (c2-0x60) with the high bit left clear, so 'und' is 0x55C4 = 21956 and 'eng' is 0x55C1 = 22017. The template switches interpretation at value < 0x0400 (line 276), so values from 0x0400 up are read as packed letters. A generator should emit from both halves and also from the gap around 0x0400, where the two interpretations meet and readers disagree. 32767 is qtlUnspecified and is special-cased by the same line.

qtopcolor.red.tier_rationale: The red component of the video media header's chroma-key colour is stored and never validated; the prompt names colour values as Tier C outright, and pinning it would make every vmhd identical.
qtopcolor.red.description: Red component of the opcolor used with the video media header's graphics mode.
qtopcolor.red.notes: Meaningful only for the transparency and blend graphics modes; for the ordinary copy mode a reader ignores it entirely, which is why it is free in both cases.

qtopcolor.green.tier_rationale: A colour component the reader stores without validating; constraining it costs variation and reaches nothing.

qtopcolor.blue.tier_rationale: A colour component the reader stores without validating; constraining it costs variation and reaches nothing.

elst_entry.duration.tier_rationale: The length of one edit segment in movie timescale units; a reader clamps or ignores an implausible value rather than refusing the file, and pinning it would collapse every edit list onto one shape.
elst_entry.duration.description: Duration of this edit segment, expressed in the movie timescale from the mvhd box.

evidence.snippet: uint32 duration <name="Duration", comment="Duration of this edit segment in movie time scale units (specified in mvhd box)">;

elst_entry.duration.notes: Zero is meaningful and must stay reachable: a zero-duration edit is how some writers mark an empty list. An edit duration longer than the track's own duration is accepted and reaches the clamping code in ffmpeg's edit-list handling, which is a genuinely separate path from the ordinary case.

elst_entry.media_time.tier_rationale: The start point of this edit in media timescale units, with the sentinel value meaning an empty edit; no reader refuses any value, and pinning it would delete both the empty-edit and the offset-start paths.
elst_entry.media_time.description: Start time of this edit segment in the media timescale, or the all-ones sentinel meaning an empty edit that inserts blank presentation time.

evidence.snippet: uint32 media_time <name="Media Time", comment="Start time of this edit segment in media time scale units (specified in mdhd box)">;

elst_entry.media_time.notes: The template declares this unsigned, but ISO/IEC 14496-12 defines it as signed, so the value 0xFFFFFFFF is the sentinel -1 meaning an empty edit. That sentinel is the single most interesting value this field can take -- ffmpeg uses it to insert presentation delay and it drives a whole branch of the edit-list code -- so it must be emitted, and it is precisely the value a generator restricted to small numbers would never produce.

elst_entry.media_rate.tier_rationale: The playback rate for this edit as a 16.16 fixed-point value; unvalidated, and the special value 0 marks a dwell edit, so constraining it would delete that branch.
elst_entry.media_rate.description: Relative rate at which to play this edit segment; 0x00010000 is normal speed and 0 marks a dwell.

evidence.snippet: fp32 media_rate <name="Media Rate", comment="Relative rate at which to play this edit segment">;

elst_entry.media_rate.notes: 0 (dwell), 0x00010000 (normal) and negative values (reverse) are three different paths; none is excluded.

tkhd_flags.dummy.tier_rationale: These are the top sixteen bits of the track header's 24-bit flags word, which ISO/IEC 14496-12 leaves undefined and no reader inspects; per the rule for reserved fields nobody checks, they stay free and setting them is a cheap way to vary the header.
tkhd_flags.dummy.description: The two high bytes of the tkhd flags field, holding no defined flag.
tkhd_flags.dummy.notes: The spec expects these to be zero; because nothing validates them they are Tier C rather than a pinned zero, and a non-zero value reaches a conformance checker's reserved-bit reporting.

tkhd_flags.dummy2.tier_rationale: The upper four bits of the low flags byte carry no defined meaning and no reader inspects them, so they stay free.
tkhd_flags.dummy2.description: The four undefined high bits of the tkhd flags low byte.

bitfield.packing: big-endian bitfields fill from the most significant bit down, so these are bits 7 through 4 of the third flags byte

tkhd_flags.track_in_poster.tier_rationale: A reader that does not build poster frames ignores this bit entirely and never refuses the file, so it is not a front gate; but it is a one-bit flag with two defined meanings and a QuickTime-aware reader takes a different path for each.
tkhd_flags.track_in_poster.description: Whether this track is used when building the movie's poster frame.

bitfield.packing: bit 3 of the low flags byte, which is flag value 0x000008

tkhd_flags.track_in_preview.tier_rationale: Ignored by readers that do not build previews and never a cause of refusal; a two-valued flag whose values select different preview handling.
tkhd_flags.track_in_preview.description: Whether this track is used in the movie's preview.

bitfield.packing: bit 2 of the low flags byte, flag value 0x000004

tkhd_flags.track_in_movie.tier_rationale: A reader that honours it skips the track's presentation rather than refusing the file; two defined values selecting whether the track participates in the movie at all.
tkhd_flags.track_in_movie.description: Whether this track is used in the movie's presentation.

bitfield.packing: bit 1 of the low flags byte, flag value 0x000002

tkhd_flags.track_enabled.tier_rationale: ffmpeg reads this bit and marks a track with it clear as disabled, but it still creates the stream and still demuxes, so it is not a front gate; the two values select whether the track is presented by default, which is a real branch in every player.
tkhd_flags.track_enabled.description: Whether this track is enabled; a disabled track is present in the file but not played by default.

bitfield.packing: bit 0 of the low flags byte, flag value 0x000001

tkhd_flags.track_enabled.notes: 1 is named first because an enabled track is the one a player actually decodes, which is where the depth is; but 0 must also be generated, since ffmpeg sets AV_DISPOSITION_DEFAULT differently and some readers skip the track entirely, which is a whole branch that an always-enabled corpus never reaches.

vmhd_flags.dummy.tier_rationale: The top sixteen bits of the video media header's 24-bit flags word carry no defined flag and no reader inspects them, so they stay free.
vmhd_flags.dummy.description: The two high bytes of the vmhd flags field.

vmhd_flags.dummy2.tier_rationale: The upper seven bits of the low flags byte carry no defined meaning and nothing inspects them.
vmhd_flags.dummy2.description: The seven undefined high bits of the vmhd flags low byte.

bitfield.packing: bits 7 through 1 of the low flags byte

vmhd_flags.no_lean_ahead.tier_rationale: ISO/IEC 14496-12 states that the vmhd flags word shall be 1, which sets this bit, but ffmpeg ignores the vmhd flags entirely and was measured to demux and decode unaffected either way, so by the literal Tier A test it is not a front gate and the legal set is the two values of a single bit.
vmhd_flags.no_lean_ahead.description: The single defined bit of the video media header flags; the spec requires it set, and QuickTime names it the no-lean-ahead bit.

bitfield.packing: bit 0 of the low flags byte, giving the whole flags word the value 1

vmhd_flags.no_lean_ahead.notes: 1 is preferred because it is what every real file carries and what a strict conformance checker requires; 0 is kept in valid_values deliberately rather than dropped, because it is the only way to reach a conformance checker's vmhd-flags complaint and it was measured not to affect playback.

str_stsc.first_chunk.tier_rationale: The sample-to-chunk table is run-length coded and this field is the run boundary; a demuxer walks the entries expecting strictly increasing chunk numbers starting at 1, and a value that breaks that makes ffmpeg's index builder produce a wrong or empty sample index, so no frames are extracted.
str_stsc.first_chunk.description: The one-based index of the first chunk that uses this entry's chunk layout; the entry applies until the next entry's first_chunk.
str_stsc.first_chunk.algorithm: run-length boundary: the first entry must be 1, and each subsequent entry's value must be strictly greater than the previous entry's and no greater than the chunk count declared by stco or co64
str_stsc.first_chunk.covers: nothing in the byte stream; it indexes the chunk list that stco or co64 declares
str_stsc.first_chunk.notes: The simplest correct table is a single entry of (1, samples_per_chunk, 1), which puts every sample in one chunk; that was the form used in the verified hand-built file. How many entries to write and how the samples are distributed across chunks is free and is a real diversity axis -- many small chunks and one large chunk drive different paths through the index builder.

str_stsc.samples_per_chunk.tier_rationale: How many samples share a chunk is a count that a careful reader is tempted to fix at 1; it decides how the index builder distributes samples across chunk offsets, and pinning it would leave the multi-sample chunk arithmetic unexercised.
str_stsc.samples_per_chunk.description: The number of samples in each chunk covered by this entry.
str_stsc.samples_per_chunk.notes: Zero is representable and reaches a divide-or-loop guard in the index builder; the sum over all entries must account for every sample the stsz table declares, which is recorded as a dependency rather than pinned here.

str_stsc.sample_description_index.tier_rationale: A one-based index into the stsd entry list; an out-of-range index makes a demuxer fall back on the first description rather than refuse the file, and that fallback is the only branch an always-valid index never reaches.
str_stsc.sample_description_index.description: Which stsd sample entry describes the samples in these chunks, counted from 1.
str_stsc.sample_description_index.notes: The conforming span is 1 up to the stsd entry_count, which is recorded as a dependency; 0 and out-of-range values are accepted and reach the fallback.

str_stts.sample_count.tier_rationale: The time-to-sample table is run-length coded and this is a run length; it is a count whose variation decides how many runs the decoder walks, and pinning it would collapse every timing table onto one entry.
str_stts.sample_count.description: How many consecutive samples share this entry's duration.
str_stts.sample_count.notes: The sum over all entries should equal the total sample count from stsz; a disagreement is accepted by ffmpeg and reaches its timing-mismatch handling, so both cases are worth generating and neither field is pinned to the other. Zero is representable and produces a zero-length run, a distinct case.

str_stts.sample_delta.tier_rationale: The per-sample duration in media timescale units; a reader computes timestamps from it without validating it, and pinning it would give every generated file a constant frame rate, deleting the variable-frame-rate paths.
str_stts.sample_delta.description: The duration of each sample in this run, in media timescale units.
str_stts.sample_delta.notes: Zero is meaningful and must stay reachable: zero-duration samples are legal and force a demuxer down its coincident-timestamp path. Very large deltas relative to the timescale produce multi-hour durations and exercise the 64-bit timestamp arithmetic.

str_stsd.contentSize.tier_rationale: This is the length prefix of a sample description record and the bound of the byte array that follows it; a wrong value puts every later record at the wrong offset, and the measured consequence of a bad sample-entry length is that ffmpeg creates no stream at all.
str_stsd.contentSize.description: Total size in bytes of one sample description record, counting this field itself.
str_stsd.contentSize.algorithm: 4 for this field plus the byte count of the content array that follows
str_stsd.contentSize.size_identity: sizeof(content) == contentSize - 4, exactly as declared at line 443
str_stsd.contentSize.notes: str_stsd is defined at lines 440-449 but never instantiated: the line that would use it, line 666, is commented out in favour of line 667, which parses stsd entries as nested mp4box values instead. The record it describes is the same sample entry that mp4box.entries carries, so the real constraint lives there.

str_stsd.content.tier_rationale: These bytes are the body of a sample entry, and a sample entry whose body is malformed or truncated was MEASURED to make ffmpeg create no stream at all, so the whole decode path is lost.
str_stsd.content.description: The body of one sample description record, following its length prefix.
str_stsd.content.codec: ISO/IEC 14496-12 SampleEntry, plus the codec-specific configuration box it contains
str_stsd.content.must_produce: the same structure as mp4box.entries -- a four-character format code, six reserved bytes, a data_reference_index, then the VisualSampleEntry or AudioSampleEntry fixed fields and the nested configuration box
str_stsd.content.decoder_gate: identical to mp4box.entries; see that entry for the measured behaviour
str_stsd.content.generation_strategy: see mp4box.entries for the byte-by-byte construction; this struct is dead code in the template as it stands and a generator should build sample entries through mp4box.entries instead
str_stsd.content.notes: confidence is medium only because the struct is unreferenced, so the exact framing it expects cannot be confirmed against the template's own parse; the underlying format requirement is certain and is recorded in full on mp4box.entries.

str_sidx.reference_size31_type1.tier_rationale: A segment index with wrong reference sizes makes a streaming client seek to the wrong byte ranges, but ffmpeg reads the sidx as a hint and still demuxes the file normally, so it is not a front gate; the field is two packed subfields whose layout is fixed.
str_sidx.reference_size31_type1.description: One segment index reference, packing a one-bit reference type and a 31-bit referenced size into a single 32-bit word.

valid_bits.0x80000000: reference_type: 0 means the reference points at media (a moof plus its mdat), 1 means it points at another sidx box, which is the hierarchical-index case and a separate code path in every client
valid_bits.0x7FFFFFFF: referenced_size: the byte count of the referenced material, which for a conforming file equals the total size of the boxes it covers

str_sidx.reference_size31_type1.notes: valid_values is empty because the 31-bit size subfield spans its whole width and must not be narrowed -- it is a length and its value follows from whatever the generator actually wrote. The one-bit type subfield is the part with a finite set, and both of its values must be emitted: type 1 is the only route into a client's nested-index handling.

str_sidx.subsegment_duration.tier_rationale: The duration of one subsegment in the sidx timescale; a client uses it for seeking and never refuses a file over it, so pinning it would give every segment index the same shape for nothing.
str_sidx.subsegment_duration.description: Duration of the referenced subsegment, in the timescale the sidx box declares.
str_sidx.subsegment_duration.notes: Zero is representable and makes a client's seek arithmetic divide by zero or take its guard, which is a branch no positive value reaches.

str_sidx.SAP_delta_time28_type3_starts_w.tier_rationale: The stream access point description is advisory -- a client that ignores it still plays the file and ffmpeg does not refuse anything over it -- but the word packs three subfields with a fixed layout, and the SAP type in particular selects different seek behaviour.
str_sidx.SAP_delta_time28_type3_starts_w.description: One segment index access-point descriptor, packing a starts-with-SAP flag, a three-bit SAP type and a 28-bit delta time into a single 32-bit word.

valid_bits.0x80000000: starts_with_SAP: 1 means the subsegment begins at a stream access point, 0 means it does not and the client must decode from an earlier point
valid_bits.0x70000000: SAP_type: 0 means unknown, 1 and 2 are closed GOP access points, 3 is an open GOP, 4 is a gradual decoding refresh, and 5 and 6 are defined but rarely produced; every value 0 through 7 is representable and selects different client seek handling
valid_bits.0x0FFFFFFF: SAP_delta_time: the offset from the subsegment start to the access point, which is 0 whenever starts_with_SAP is 1

str_sidx.SAP_delta_time28_type3_starts_w.notes: valid_values is empty because the 28-bit delta is a free quantity that must not be narrowed. The three-bit SAP type is the finite part and all eight of its values should be emitted, including the reserved 7, which reaches a client's unknown-SAP fallback.

mp4box.codingName.tier_rationale: The original format code recorded by a frma box inside a protection scheme; a reader that does not recognise it treats the track as an unknown codec rather than refusing the file, so it is not a front gate, but it is a registered four-character enumeration that names which decoder to use once decryption is undone.
mp4box.codingName.description: The four-character code of the original, unencrypted sample format, stored as a 32-bit word in the frma box.
mp4box.codingName.completeness_reason: Any four-character sample format code may appear here and the registry is open-ended; the values above are the ones a reader maps to a decoder. Unregistered codes are legal and reach the unknown-codec path, which must also be generated.
mp4box.codingName.notes: The template declares this as a uint32 rather than a fourcc (line 500), so the decimal values above are the big-endian packings of the four ASCII characters: 'avc1' is 0x61766331 = 1635148593 and 'mp4a' is 0x6D703461 = 1836069985. A generator should write the four characters and let the packing follow.

mp4box.version.tier_rationale: A version a reader does not know makes it skip the box body rather than refuse the file, so it is not a front gate; but every full box in this template branches on it to choose between 32-bit and 64-bit field widths, so the two values produce structurally different boxes.
mp4box.version.description: The version byte of a full box, which selects the width of that box's time and offset fields.
mp4box.version.applies_when: declared in twenty-seven switch arms -- tenc (503), schm (518), pssh (525), senc (540), saio (558), saiz (572), trun (588), tfhd (611), mfhd (621), sidx (626), trex (645), mehd (654), stsd (663), enca (670), stts (676), stsc (682), stco (688), co64 (694), stsz (700), stss (710), elst (716), hdlr (730), mdhd (741), mvhd (751), smhd (770), tkhd (776) and vmhd (793)

per_box_semantics.saio: version 0 gives 32-bit offsets and version 1 gives 64-bit offsets (lines 566-569)
per_box_semantics.sidx: version 0 gives 32-bit earliest_presentation_time and first_offset, version 1 gives 64-bit (lines 630-639)
per_box_semantics.mehd: version 0 gives a 32-bit fragment_duration and version 1 a 64-bit one (lines 656-659)
per_box_semantics.trun: version 0 makes sample_composition_time_offset unsigned and version 1 makes it signed, which is how negative composition offsets are expressed (lines 602-605)
per_box_semantics.pssh: version above 0 adds the KID_count and KID array (lines 528-535)
per_box_semantics.tenc: version 0 gives a second reserved byte and any other version gives default_crypt_skip_byte_block instead (lines 506-507)
per_box_semantics.mvhd, tkhd, mdhd: the template only models version 0 for these three, so a version 1 box -- which the spec defines with 64-bit times -- would be misparsed by this template even though real readers handle it

mp4box.version.notes: Both values must be emitted. Version 1 is the only route into every 64-bit field width in the format and into pssh's key-identifier list, and version 0 is the only route into the 32-bit paths; a corpus fixed at 0 leaves half of the sample-table and fragment code unreached. Values above 1 are representable and reach a reader's unknown-version skip, which is also worth generating, but they are not listed as legal because the spec defines only 0 and 1 for these boxes.

mp4box.flag.tier_rationale: In trun, tfhd, saio and saiz these three bytes are not decoration: each bit declares whether an optional field is physically present, so a bit that disagrees with the bytes actually written shifts every following field and the box, and everything after it, is parsed at the wrong offset.
mp4box.flag.description: The 24-bit flags word of a full box, written most significant byte first, whose bits select which optional fields the box body contains.

valid_bits.trun flag[1] & 0x01: sample-duration-present: adds uint32 sample_duration to every entry (line 597)
valid_bits.trun flag[1] & 0x02: sample-size-present: adds uint32 sample_size to every entry (line 598)
valid_bits.trun flag[1] & 0x04: sample-flags-present: adds uint32 sample_flags to every entry (line 599)
valid_bits.trun flag[1] & 0x08: sample-composition-time-offsets-present: adds a 32-bit composition offset to every entry, signed when version is 1 (lines 600-606)
valid_bits.tfhd flag[0] & 0x01: duration-is-empty: declares the fragment has no samples; the template does not model it but readers honour it
valid_bits.tfhd flag[0] & 0x02: default-base-is-moof: bases offsets on the enclosing moof rather than the file, which is the standard DASH configuration and a separate addressing path
valid_bits.saio flag[2] & 0x01 and saiz flag[2] & 0: aux-info-type-present: adds the aux_info_type and its parameter (lines 560-564 and 574-578)
valid_bits.senc flag[2] & 0x02: use-subsample-encryption: adds the subsample_count and subsample_data array to every entry (lines 546-554)
valid_bits.dref url flag[2] & 0x01: self-contained: the media is in this file and no URL string follows, which is what nearly every real file uses
valid_bits.all other bits: undefined for these boxes and ignored; for the boxes whose bodies are fixed the whole word is ignored

mp4box.flag.applies_when: declared in twenty switch arms; the bit meanings above apply to trun, tfhd, saio, saiz and senc, while in stsd, stts, stsc, stco, co64, stsz, stss, mfhd, sidx, trex, mehd, pssh, schm, tenc and enca the word has no defined bits and is ignored
mp4box.flag.notes: valid_values is empty because this is a presence bitmask, not a value set: the legal combinations are every subset of the defined bits, and a generator must vary which optional fields it emits and set exactly the matching bits. That variation is itself a major diversity axis -- a trun with all four per-sample fields present exercises completely different code from one with none -- so the bits must not be fixed to a single combination. Note one template quirk: line 546 tests senc's subsample bit with flag[2] == 2 rather than a bit test, so a senc box whose flags are 0x000003 would not have its subsamples parsed by this template even though a reader would parse them.

mp4box.reserved1.tier_rationale: The first reserved byte of the track encryption box, which ISO/IEC 23001-7 requires to be zero but which no reader inspects; per the rule for reserved fields nobody checks, it stays free.
mp4box.reserved1.description: The reserved byte immediately after the tenc box's version and flags.

mp4box.reserved2.tier_rationale: Declared twice, as a tenc reserved byte present only at version 0 and as the 64-bit reserved field of the track header; neither is inspected by any reader, so both stay free.
mp4box.reserved2.description: A reserved field: one byte in tenc when version is 0 (line 506), or eight bytes in tkhd (line 783).
mp4box.reserved2.applies_when: tenc at line 506, where it exists only when version is 0 and is replaced by default_crypt_skip_byte_block otherwise; and tkhd at line 783, where it is a uint64 the spec requires to be zero
mp4box.reserved2.notes: In tkhd this eight-byte field occupies the position the QuickTime specification gives to the track's reserved words; ffmpeg skips it without reading. Setting it non-zero is accepted and reaches a conformance checker's reserved-field reporting.

mp4box.default_crypt_skip_byte_block.tier_rationale: The packed crypt and skip byte-block counts used by the pattern encryption schemes; a decryptor reads them but a demuxer never refuses a file over them, and pinning them would delete every pattern-encryption path.
mp4box.default_crypt_skip_byte_block.description: A byte packing the default crypt byte block count in its high nibble and the skip byte block count in its low nibble, present in tenc when version is not 0.
mp4box.default_crypt_skip_byte_block.notes: The common patterns are 1:9 (0x19) and 5:5 (0x55) for cbcs, and 0:0 (0x00) for full-sample encryption; all 256 packings are representable and a decryptor branches on whether either nibble is zero, so the field stays free.

mp4box.default_is_protected.tier_rationale: A value outside the defined pair makes a decryptor treat the track as unprotected rather than refuse the file, so it is not a front gate; the two defined values select whether the decryption path runs at all.
mp4box.default_is_protected.description: Whether samples in this track are encrypted by default.
mp4box.default_is_protected.notes: Both matter: 1 is the only route into the decryption setup and the per-sample IV handling, while 0 with a sinf box present is the clear-lead case that readers handle separately.

mp4box.default_per_sample_IV_size.tier_rationale: A size a decryptor does not recognise makes it reject the encryption setup for the track rather than refuse the container, so it is not a front gate; the defined set is three values and the template branches on one of them at line 511 to decide whether a constant IV follows.
mp4box.default_per_sample_IV_size.description: The byte length of the per-sample initialisation vector; zero means there is no per-sample IV and a constant IV follows instead.
value_names: no per-sample IV, a constant IV follows
mp4box.default_per_sample_IV_size.notes: All three are preferred. Zero is structurally the most interesting because it is the only value that brings default_constant_IV_size and default_constant_IV into existence (lines 511-515), changing the box's layout entirely; 8 and 16 are the two IV widths a decryptor handles with different code.

mp4box.default_KID.tier_rationale: A sixteen-byte key identifier that a decryptor matches against its key store; no value makes a demuxer refuse the file, and pinning it would make every protected file reference the same key.
mp4box.default_KID.description: The default key identifier for samples in this track, as a sixteen-byte value.
mp4box.default_KID.notes: The all-zero identifier is meaningful -- it signals that no default key applies -- and must stay reachable, so nothing is excluded.

mp4box.default_constant_IV_size.tier_rationale: This byte is the array bound for the constant IV that immediately follows it at line 514, so a value that disagrees with the bytes written leaves the parser inside the tenc box and every field and box after it is read at the wrong offset.
mp4box.default_constant_IV_size.description: The byte length of the constant initialisation vector, present only when default_per_sample_IV_size is zero.
mp4box.default_constant_IV_size.algorithm: byte count of the default_constant_IV array that follows
mp4box.default_constant_IV_size.size_identity: sizeof(default_constant_IV) == default_constant_IV_size, as declared at line 514
mp4box.default_constant_IV_size.notes: ISO/IEC 23001-7 permits only 8 and 16 here, but the field is a free byte and a decryptor rejects other widths while the container still parses, so the identity with the array is what matters and is Tier A. Which of the two legal widths to use is free.

mp4box.default_constant_IV.tier_rationale: The constant initialisation vector's bytes are opaque key material that no parser inspects; constraining them would remove variation and reach nothing.
mp4box.default_constant_IV.description: The constant initialisation vector used for every sample when there is no per-sample IV.

mp4box.scheme_type.tier_rationale: A scheme a reader does not know makes it leave the track encrypted and report an unsupported scheme rather than refuse the file, so it is not a front gate; the Common Encryption schemes are a closed four-value set and each selects a different cipher and block layout.
mp4box.scheme_type.description: The four-character protection scheme identifier from the schm box, stored as a 32-bit word.
mp4box.scheme_type.completeness_reason: The four Common Encryption schemes are the complete set that standard defines, but the field is a free four-character code and other protection systems register their own, so unregistered values are legal and reach the unsupported-scheme path.
mp4box.scheme_type.notes: The decimal values are the big-endian packings of the four ASCII characters: 'cenc' is 0x63656E63 = 1667591779 and 'cbcs' is 0x63626373 = 1667392371. cenc and cbcs are named as preferred because they are the two schemes real content uses, but cbc1 and cens must be generated too -- each has its own cipher and pattern handling.

mp4box.scheme_version.tier_rationale: The scheme version is stored and compared only by systems that implement that scheme; a demuxer never refuses a file over it, and pinning it would remove the only variation the schm box has left.
mp4box.scheme_version.description: The version of the protection scheme, conventionally packed as a major and minor 16-bit pair.
mp4box.scheme_version.notes: The conventional value is 0x00010000 for version 1.0, but any 32-bit value parses and a reader that checks it takes its version-mismatch branch, which no fixed value reaches.

mp4box.systemID.tier_rationale: A DRM system identifier the player does not know makes it skip that pssh box and look for another, rather than refuse the file, so it is not a front gate; but the registered identifiers are a finite set and each one routes the box to a different key system.
mp4box.systemID.description: The sixteen-byte UUID identifying which DRM system the protection header belongs to.
valid_values: urn:uuid values not listed are equally legal
mp4box.systemID.completeness_reason: The DASH-IF registry of system identifiers grows continuously and the field is sixteen free bytes, so no list is closed; those above are the systems players actually branch on. Unregistered UUIDs are legal and reach the skip-this-pssh path, which must also be generated.
mp4box.systemID.notes: The values are written as the sixteen raw bytes in big-endian UUID order, not as text. Clear Key is the highest-value identifier for a test corpus because it is the one system every EME implementation supports without a licence server.

mp4box.KID_count.tier_rationale: This is the array bound for the sixteen-byte key identifiers that follow it at line 534, so a value that disagrees with the entries written leaves the parser inside the pssh box and the DataSize and Data that follow are read from the wrong offset.
mp4box.KID_count.description: The number of key identifiers listed in a version 1 or later pssh box.
mp4box.KID_count.algorithm: count of the sixteen-byte KID entries written into the array that follows
mp4box.KID_count.covers: nothing in the byte stream; it is the element count of the array declared at line 534, so the array occupies 16 * KID_count bytes
mp4box.KID_count.size_identity: sizeof(KID) == 16 * KID_count; present only when version is greater than 0, which the template tests at line 528
mp4box.KID_count.notes: Tier A as an identity, not as a pinned number: HOW MANY key identifiers to list is entirely free and is a real diversity axis, since zero, one and many identifiers take different paths through a player's key-matching code. This field simply records the choice.

mp4box.entry.tier_rationale: Declared four times as the element of a repeating table -- a pssh key identifier, a saiz per-sample size, and the stts and stsc records -- whose contents are either opaque key material or covered by their own struct entries; nothing here is validated in a way that would make a reader refuse the file.
mp4box.entry.description: One element of a repeating table: a sixteen-byte key identifier in pssh (line 533), a one-byte auxiliary info size in saiz (line 583), or a time-to-sample or sample-to-chunk record in stts and stsc (lines 679 and 685).
mp4box.entry.applies_when: pssh KID entries at line 533, saiz per-sample sizes at line 583, stts records at line 679 and stsc records at line 685; the stts and stsc record fields carry their own constraints under str_stts and str_stsc
mp4box.entry.notes: In saiz this byte is the per-sample auxiliary information size and is present only when default_sample_info_size is zero (line 581); a zero entry there means that sample has no auxiliary data, which is a legal and separately handled case.

mp4box.KID.tier_rationale: The key identifier array of a pssh box is opaque key material a player matches against its key store; no value makes a demuxer refuse the file, and pinning it would make every protected file reference the same keys.
mp4box.KID.description: The array of sixteen-byte key identifiers in a version 1 or later pssh box.
mp4box.KID.size_identity: the array holds KID_count elements of 16 bytes each; the count is constrained under mp4box.KID_count

mp4box.DataSize.tier_rationale: This is the array bound for the protection system data that follows it at line 537 and the last field before the box ends, so a value that disagrees with the bytes written leaves the parser inside the pssh box and the next box is read from the wrong offset.
mp4box.DataSize.description: The byte length of the DRM system specific data that follows in a pssh box.
mp4box.DataSize.algorithm: byte count of the mp4box.Data array that follows
mp4box.DataSize.size_identity: sizeof(Data) == DataSize, as declared at line 537, and the pssh box size must equal 12 + 16 + (version > 0 ? 4 + 16 * KID_count : 0) + 4 + DataSize
mp4box.DataSize.notes: Zero is legal and common -- a pssh box that carries only key identifiers and no system data has DataSize 0 -- so it is not excluded.

mp4box.Data.tier_rationale: These bytes are DRM system specific and completely opaque to the container: ffmpeg copies them into side data without parsing, and no value makes a demuxer refuse the file, so constraining them would remove variation without reaching a single container line.
mp4box.Data.description: The protection system specific data of a pssh box, whose meaning is defined by the DRM system the systemID names.
mp4box.Data.notes: Asked the question the checklist requires -- what must be inside this? The answer is: nothing, as far as any container parser is concerned. The DRM systems do impose structure on their own data (Widevine uses a protocol buffer whose first byte is typically 0x08, PlayReady a little-endian length followed by UTF-16LE XML, Clear Key a list of raw sixteen-byte key identifiers), and emitting those shapes reaches a player's key-system parsing, so they are worth producing for the systemID in use. But none of it is a container gate, which is why this is Tier C rather than a payload_wellformedness entry.

mp4box.sample_count.tier_rationale: In senc, trun and saiz this is the bound of a loop that reads per-sample records, and in stsz it is the bound of the sample-size table; a value larger than the records written makes the parser read past the box into whatever follows, and a smaller one leaves records unconsumed so the next box is read from inside the table.
mp4box.sample_count.description: The number of per-sample records that follow: encryption entries in senc, run entries in trun, auxiliary sizes in saiz, or sample sizes in stsz.
mp4box.sample_count.algorithm: count of the per-sample records actually written into the array or loop that follows
mp4box.sample_count.covers: nothing in the byte stream; it is the element count for the entry array at line 555, the for loop at line 593, the saiz entry array at line 583 or the stsz entry_size array at line 706

per_box_semantics.senc: bounds the entry array at line 555, each element being an eight-byte IV and, when the subsample bit is set, a subsample table
per_box_semantics.saiz: bounds the byte array at line 583, but only when default_sample_info_size is zero (line 581)
per_box_semantics.trun: bounds the for loop at line 593 whose body's size depends entirely on which flag bits are set, so the same count produces wildly different byte lengths
per_box_semantics.stsz: declares how many samples the track has, and bounds the entry_size array at line 706 only when sample_size is zero (line 704)

mp4box.sample_count.size_identity: in trun the bytes consumed are sample_count multiplied by the sum of 4 for each of the four per-sample flag bits that are set; in stsz they are 4 * sample_count when sample_size is 0 and nothing otherwise
mp4box.sample_count.measured_gate: MEASURED: zeroing every entry in a stsz table left ffmpeg creating the stream but reading zero frames, so the sample count and sizes together are what turn a parsed container into decoded output.
mp4box.sample_count.notes: Tier A as an identity, not as a pinned number: HOW MANY samples a track has is entirely the generator's choice, is where a corpus's duration and complexity diversity comes from, and is bounded only by the output_budget on the box sequence. This field records the choice.

mp4box.per_sample_IV.tier_rationale: An eight-byte initialisation vector per encrypted sample; it is opaque key material a decryptor consumes and no parser validates, so pinning it would remove variation and reach nothing.
mp4box.per_sample_IV.description: The initialisation vector for one encrypted sample in a senc box.
mp4box.per_sample_IV.notes: The template fixes this at eight bytes (line 545), but ISO/IEC 23001-7 lets the width follow the tenc box's default_per_sample_IV_size, so a file with a sixteen-byte IV would be misparsed by this template even though readers handle it. That mismatch is recorded as a dependency.

mp4box.subsample_count.tier_rationale: This is the bound of the subsample table that immediately follows it at line 553, so a value that disagrees with the records written leaves the parser inside the senc entry and every later sample's encryption record is read at the wrong offset.
mp4box.subsample_count.description: The number of clear-and-protected byte ranges that make up one partially encrypted sample.
mp4box.subsample_count.algorithm: count of the six-byte subsample records written into the array that follows
mp4box.subsample_count.covers: nothing in the byte stream; it is the element count of the array at line 553, which occupies 6 * subsample_count bytes
mp4box.subsample_count.size_identity: each subsample record is a uint16 plus a uint32, so exactly 6 bytes; the array occupies 6 * subsample_count bytes and exists only when the senc subsample flag bit is set, which the template tests at line 546
mp4box.subsample_count.notes: Tier A as an identity; the number of subsample ranges per sample is free and is what makes partially encrypted video differ from fully encrypted video in a decryptor's inner loop.

mp4box.bytes_of_clear_data.tier_rationale: The length of one unencrypted run inside a partially encrypted sample; a decryptor uses it to step through the sample and no parser refuses a file over it, so pinning it would collapse every subsample layout onto one shape.
mp4box.bytes_of_clear_data.description: How many bytes at the start of this subsample range are left in the clear.
mp4box.bytes_of_clear_data.notes: Zero is meaningful and common -- it means the range is entirely encrypted -- so it is not excluded. The sum of the clear and protected lengths across a sample's subsamples should equal that sample's size, which is recorded as a dependency rather than pinned here.

mp4box.bytes_of_protected_data.tier_rationale: The length of one encrypted run inside a partially encrypted sample; unvalidated by any parser, and zero is meaningful, so constraining it would delete both the fully-clear and the mixed cases.
mp4box.bytes_of_protected_data.description: How many bytes after the clear run of this subsample range are encrypted.

mp4box.aux_info_type.tier_rationale: An auxiliary information type a reader does not know makes it ignore the saiz or saio box rather than refuse the file, so it is not a front gate; but the registered types are a small set and each names a different kind of per-sample side data.
mp4box.aux_info_type.description: The four-character code naming what kind of auxiliary information the saiz or saio box sizes and locates.
mp4box.aux_info_type.completeness_reason: The Common Encryption types above are the ones defined for this field in practice, but it is a free four-character code and other specifications may register their own; unregistered values are legal and reach the ignore path.
mp4box.aux_info_type.applies_when: saio at line 562 and saiz at line 576, in both cases present only when bit 0 of the flags word is set
mp4box.aux_info_type.notes: Present only when the aux-info-type-present flag bit is set, which the template tests at lines 560 and 574; whether to set that bit is itself free and changes the box's layout.

mp4box.aud_info_type_parameter.tier_rationale: A free parameter qualifying the auxiliary information type; readers pass it through without validation, so constraining it reaches nothing.
mp4box.aud_info_type_parameter.description: The parameter qualifying the saio box's auxiliary information type.
mp4box.aud_info_type_parameter.notes: The field name is spelled aud_info_type_parameter at line 563, which is a typo in the template for aux_info_type_parameter; the saiz box spells the same field correctly at line 577, so the two boxes have differently named keys for the same concept. The spelling is reproduced exactly as the template has it.

mp4box.entry_count.tier_rationale: This is the array bound for every table box in the format, and it is the hardest measured gate in MP4: a stsd entry_count that disagrees with the entries actually present makes ffmpeg abort with 'invalid size 5 in stsd' and create NO STREAM AT ALL, so nothing is demuxed and nothing is decoded.
mp4box.entry_count.description: The number of records that follow in a table box: sample descriptions, time-to-sample runs, sample-to-chunk runs, chunk offsets, sync samples, or auxiliary information offsets.
mp4box.entry_count.algorithm: count of the records actually written into the array that follows
mp4box.entry_count.covers: nothing in the byte stream; it is the element count for the array declared immediately after it in each box
mp4box.entry_count.applies_when: saio (565), stsd (665), enca (672), stts (678), stsc (684), stco (690), co64 (696) and stss (712)

per_box_semantics.stsd: bounds the nested sample-entry boxes at line 667; each entry is a whole box with its own size, so the count and the sizes must agree with each other and with the stsd box size
per_box_semantics.stts: bounds the str_stts run array at line 679, 8 bytes per record
per_box_semantics.stsc: bounds the str_stsc run array at line 685, 12 bytes per record
per_box_semantics.stco: bounds the 32-bit chunk offset array at line 691, 4 bytes per record
per_box_semantics.co64: bounds the 64-bit chunk offset array at line 697, 8 bytes per record
per_box_semantics.stss: bounds the sync sample number array at line 713, 4 bytes per record
per_box_semantics.saio: bounds the offset array at line 567 or 569, 4 or 8 bytes per record depending on version
per_box_semantics.enca: declared at line 672 but followed by a fixed 20-byte array rather than a table, so it bounds nothing in this template

mp4box.entry_count.size_identity: for the fixed-width tables the array occupies entry_count multiplied by the record width above; for stsd the entries are variable-length boxes and the identity is that their sizes sum to the stsd box size minus 16
mp4box.entry_count.measured_gate: MEASURED on a working hand-built file: setting the stsd entry_count to 5 while only one entry was present produced 'invalid size 5 in stsd' from the mov demuxer and NO STREAM AT ALL; setting the stts entry_count to 0 produced 'stream 0, missing mandatory atoms' and zero frames while still listing the stream.
mp4box.entry_count.notes: Tier A as an identity, not as a pinned number. HOW MANY records each table holds is entirely free and is one of the strongest diversity axes in the format -- a single-entry stts is a constant frame rate while a many-entry one is variable, a single-entry stco puts everything in one chunk while many entries scatter it -- and those choices are bounded only by the output_budget on the box sequence. Never pin the count; write the records first and then record how many there were.

mp4box.offset.tier_rationale: These are absolute file offsets at which a reader expects to find per-sample auxiliary information; an offset that does not point at the real data makes a decryptor read key material from the wrong place and abandon the track, so the decryption path is lost.
mp4box.offset.description: The array of file offsets locating the auxiliary information for each sample or chunk, 32-bit at version 0 and 64-bit at version 1.
mp4box.offset.algorithm: absolute byte offset from the start of the file to the auxiliary information the corresponding saiz entry sizes
mp4box.offset.covers: nothing in the byte stream; each element points into the file at the auxiliary data it locates
mp4box.offset.size_identity: the array holds entry_count elements of 4 bytes at version 0 (line 567) or 8 bytes at version 1 (line 569)
mp4box.offset.notes: Compute these last, once the file layout is settled, exactly as for stco chunk offsets. Both widths must be generated: the 64-bit form at version 1 is the only route into a reader's large-file offset handling.

mp4box.aux_info_type_parameter.tier_rationale: A free parameter qualifying the saiz box's auxiliary information type; readers pass it through without validating it.
mp4box.aux_info_type_parameter.description: The parameter qualifying the saiz box's auxiliary information type.
mp4box.aux_info_type_parameter.notes: This is the correctly spelled counterpart of mp4box.aud_info_type_parameter at line 563; the two are the same concept in two boxes, spelled differently by the template.

mp4box.default_sample_info_size.tier_rationale: A byte declaring one auxiliary size for every sample, where zero means a per-sample table follows instead; no reader refuses a file over it, and pinning it to either case would delete the other branch of the template's own test at line 581.
mp4box.default_sample_info_size.description: The auxiliary information size shared by every sample, or zero to signal that a per-sample size table follows.
mp4box.default_sample_info_size.notes: Zero is structurally the interesting value because it is the only one that brings the per-sample entry array at line 583 into existence, changing the box's length entirely; non-zero values make the box fixed-length. Both must be generated, which is a choice about layout rather than a value constraint.

mp4box.data_offset.tier_rationale: The offset from the enclosing moof or file base to the first sample of a track run; a reader uses it to locate fragment data and a wrong value costs the fragment's samples but never the container, and pinning it would delete the offset arithmetic entirely.
mp4box.data_offset.description: Offset to the first sample of this track run, present only when the data-offset flag bit is set.
mp4box.data_offset.notes: The template declares this unsigned but ISO/IEC 14496-12 defines it as signed, so values at or above 0x80000000 are negative offsets -- pointing backwards from the moof -- which is legal, is produced by real writers, and reaches a reader's signed-offset path that no small positive value can.

mp4box.first_sample_flags.tier_rationale: This word overrides the sample flags for the first sample of a run, and a reader that does not recognise a bit combination simply treats the sample conservatively rather than refusing the file; but the layout is a fixed bit packing and the sync bit in particular decides whether the sample is a keyframe.
mp4box.first_sample_flags.description: The sample flags applied to the first sample of this track run, overriding the default, present only when the first-sample-flags bit is set.

valid_bits.0x0C000000: is_leading: 0 unknown, 1 leading and decodable, 2 not leading, 3 leading and not decodable
valid_bits.0x03000000: sample_depends_on: 0 unknown, 1 depends on others (not an I-frame), 2 depends on nothing (an I-frame), 3 reserved
valid_bits.0x00C00000: sample_is_depended_on: 0 unknown, 1 others depend on this, 2 nothing depends on this (disposable), 3 reserved
valid_bits.0x00300000: sample_has_redundancy: 0 unknown, 1 redundant coding present, 2 none, 3 reserved
valid_bits.0x00010000: sample_is_non_sync_sample: set means the sample is NOT a sync sample, so clearing it is what marks a keyframe -- this is the bit ffmpeg turns into AV_PKT_FLAG_KEY

mp4box.first_sample_flags.notes: valid_values is empty because every combination of these subfields is representable and legal; the field must not be narrowed to a value set. The single highest-value bit is 0x00010000: a run whose first sample has it clear is seekable and ffmpeg builds a keyframe index entry for it, while a run with it set everywhere leaves the index empty and the seek path unreached. Generate both.

mp4box.sample_duration.tier_rationale: The per-sample duration inside a track run; a reader accumulates it into timestamps without validating it, and pinning it would give every fragment a constant frame rate, deleting the variable-rate paths.
mp4box.sample_duration.description: Duration of one sample in a track run, in media timescale units, present only when the sample-duration flag bit is set.
mp4box.sample_duration.notes: Zero is legal and forces coincident timestamps, which is a separate path; when the flag bit is clear the reader falls back on the tfhd or trex default instead, and that fallback is itself a branch worth reaching by leaving the bit clear.

mp4box.sample_size.tier_rationale: Declared both as a per-sample size inside a track run and as the stsz constant sample size; in both cases a reader uses it to step through media bytes and a wrong value costs samples but not the container, and pinning it would make every sample the same length.
mp4box.sample_size.description: In trun, the byte length of one sample in the run; in stsz, a single size shared by every sample, where zero signals that a per-sample table follows instead.
mp4box.sample_size.applies_when: trun at line 598, present only when the sample-size flag bit is set; and stsz at line 702, where it is always present

per_box_semantics.trun: the byte length of this one sample, used with data_offset to walk the fragment
per_box_semantics.stsz: a constant size for every sample; the value 0 is a sentinel meaning the sizes are individually listed in the entry_size array, which the template tests at line 704

mp4box.sample_size.notes: The stsz sentinel 0 is structurally the most interesting value in this field: it is the only one that brings the entry_size table into existence and changes the box from fixed to variable length. Both the constant-size and the table form must be generated. For a real decode the sizes must agree with the bytes actually present in mdat, which is recorded as a dependency and in meta.unnamed_payloads.

mp4box.sample_flags.tier_rationale: A reader that meets an unfamiliar combination treats the sample conservatively rather than refusing the file, so it is not a front gate; but the word is a fixed bit packing whose sync bit decides whether the sample enters the keyframe index.
mp4box.sample_flags.description: Per-sample flags inside a track run, present only when the sample-flags bit is set; same layout as first_sample_flags.

valid_bits.0x00010000: sample_is_non_sync_sample: clear marks a sync sample and is what ffmpeg turns into a keyframe flag

mp4box.sample_flags.notes: Identical layout to mp4box.first_sample_flags and mp4box.default_sample_flags; the three differ only in scope. Vary the combinations across samples rather than writing one constant, since a run in which every sample is a sync sample and one in which none is take different paths through a reader's index builder.

mp4box.sample_composition_time_offset.tier_rationale: The difference between a sample's decode and presentation time, which a reader adds to timestamps without validating; pinning it to zero would delete the entire out-of-order presentation path that B-frames depend on.
mp4box.sample_composition_time_offset.description: Offset from decode time to composition time for one sample, unsigned at version 0 and signed at version 1.
mp4box.sample_composition_time_offset.notes: Declared twice, unsigned at line 603 when version is 0 and signed at line 605 when it is not; that is the whole reason version 1 of trun exists. Negative offsets are the ones that matter -- they are how a stream with B-frames expresses presentation reordering, and they reach a reader's timestamp reordering queue that a zero-offset corpus never touches.

mp4box.trackID.tier_rationale: A track identifier that a fragment or track-extends box uses to name which track it configures; an identifier that matches no track makes a reader skip the fragment rather than refuse the file, and that mismatch branch is one an always-matching corpus never reaches.
mp4box.trackID.description: The identifier of the track this tfhd or trex box configures, matching a tkhd track_id.
mp4box.trackID.applies_when: tfhd at line 613 and trex at line 647
mp4box.trackID.notes: Zero is reserved by the spec as meaning no track, and is accepted by readers as a mismatch; it is not excluded. Whether the identifier matches an existing tkhd track_id is recorded as a dependency, because both the matching and the dangling case are worth generating.

mp4box.base_data_offset.tier_rationale: The absolute base from which a track fragment's sample offsets are measured; a wrong base costs the fragment's samples but never the container, and pinning it would delete the explicit-base addressing mode entirely.
mp4box.base_data_offset.description: Absolute file offset forming the base for this track fragment's data offsets, present only when the base-data-offset flag bit is set.
mp4box.base_data_offset.notes: Whether to set the flag bit at all is the more consequential choice: with the bit clear a reader falls back on the default-base-is-moof rule or on the end of the previous fragment, which are two further addressing modes. All three must be generated.
