mp4box.sample_description_index.tier_rationale: A one-based index selecting which stsd entry describes this fragment's samples; an out-of-range index makes a reader fall back on the first description rather than refuse the file, and that fallback is the only branch a valid index never reaches.
mp4box.sample_description_index.description: Which stsd sample entry applies to this track fragment, counted from 1.
mp4box.sample_description_index.notes: Distinct from str_stsc.sample_description_index at line 431, which does the same job for the non-fragmented sample table. The conforming span is 1 up to the stsd entry_count, recorded as a dependency.

mp4box.default_sample_duration.tier_rationale: A fallback per-sample duration used when a track run does not carry its own; unvalidated by any reader, and pinning it would give every fragment a constant frame rate.
mp4box.default_sample_duration.description: The duration applied to samples in this fragment or track that do not declare their own.
mp4box.default_sample_duration.applies_when: tfhd at line 616, present only when its flag bit is set; and trex at line 649, where it is always present
mp4box.default_sample_duration.notes: The three-level fallback -- trun's own value, then tfhd's default, then trex's default -- is a real cascade in every fragmented reader, and the only way to exercise its lower levels is to leave the higher ones absent.

mp4box.default_sample_size.tier_rationale: A fallback sample size for fragments whose runs do not declare their own; unvalidated, and pinning it would make every sample the same length and delete the fallback cascade.
mp4box.default_sample_size.description: The byte size applied to samples in this fragment or track that do not declare their own.
mp4box.default_sample_size.applies_when: tfhd at line 617, present only when its flag bit is set; and trex at line 650, where it is always present

mp4box.default_sample_flags.tier_rationale: The fallback sample flags for a fragment; a reader that meets an unfamiliar combination treats the samples conservatively rather than refusing the file, but the word is the same fixed bit packing as sample_flags and its sync bit decides keyframe indexing for every sample that has no flags of its own.
mp4box.default_sample_flags.description: The sample flags applied to samples in this fragment or track that do not declare their own.

valid_bits.0x00010000: sample_is_non_sync_sample: the conventional default is to set it, so that only the first sample of a run, via first_sample_flags, is a keyframe

mp4box.default_sample_flags.applies_when: tfhd at line 618, present only when its flag bit is set; and trex at line 651, where it is always present

mp4box.sequence_number.tier_rationale: The ordinal of a movie fragment, which a reader uses to detect gaps in a live stream; an out-of-order value makes it report a discontinuity rather than refuse the file, and that discontinuity branch is one a strictly increasing corpus never reaches.
mp4box.sequence_number.description: The sequence number of this movie fragment, conventionally increasing by one per fragment.
mp4box.sequence_number.notes: Deliberately NOT a calculated_value: unlike the APNG sequence counter, a reader tolerates gaps and repeats here and simply reports them, so the disagreeing case is a branch worth generating rather than an error to avoid.

mp4box.referenceID.tier_rationale: The stream the segment index refers to; a reference to a track that does not exist makes a client ignore the index rather than refuse the file, and pinning it would delete the dangling-reference branch.
mp4box.referenceID.description: The track identifier the segment index describes.

mp4box.timescale.tier_rationale: The time unit of the segment index, which a client divides by to convert durations; the prompt names timescales alongside sample rates as Tier C, no reader refuses any value, and zero is the only way to reach the divide-by-zero guard.
mp4box.timescale.description: Number of time units per second used by this segment index's durations.
mp4box.timescale.notes: Spelled timescale here (line 629) but time_scale in mvhd and mdhd (lines 745 and 755), so they are separate keys. Zero is not excluded; it is the value that reaches every guard in a client's duration arithmetic.

mp4box.earliest_presentation_time.tier_rationale: The presentation time of the first sample the index covers; a client uses it for seeking and never refuses a file over it, so pinning it would give every segment index the same origin.
mp4box.earliest_presentation_time.description: Presentation time of the first sample of the first subsegment, 32-bit at version 0 and 64-bit at version 1.
mp4box.earliest_presentation_time.notes: Both widths must be generated; the 64-bit form at version 1 is the only route into a client's large-timestamp arithmetic.

mp4box.first_offset.tier_rationale: The distance from the end of the segment index box to the first referenced material; a wrong value makes a client fetch the wrong byte range but never makes a demuxer refuse the file, and pinning it to zero would delete the non-adjacent-index addressing mode.
mp4box.first_offset.description: Offset from the end of this sidx box to the first byte of the first referenced subsegment, 32-bit at version 0 and 64-bit at version 1.
mp4box.first_offset.notes: Zero, meaning the referenced material begins immediately after the index, is the common case and must not become the only case.

mp4box.reserved.tier_rationale: Declared four times -- the sidx reserved half-word, the mvhd ten reserved bytes, the smhd reserved half-word and the tkhd reserved word -- all of which the spec requires to be zero and none of which any reader inspects, so per the rule for reserved fields nobody checks they stay free.
mp4box.reserved.description: A reserved field the specification requires to be zero: 2 bytes in sidx (line 640), 10 bytes in mvhd (line 759), 2 bytes in smhd (line 773) and 4 bytes in tkhd (line 781).
mp4box.reserved.applies_when: sidx (640), mvhd (759), smhd (773) and tkhd (781); all four share this key because the template declares them in one struct scope
mp4box.reserved.notes: In the sidx box the top bit of this half-word is actually reference_count's neighbour and the spec reserves the whole 16 bits; in mvhd the ten bytes are the QuickTime reserved area between preferred_volume and the matrix. None is validated, so all stay free, and non-zero values reach a conformance checker's reserved-field reporting.

mp4box.reference_count.tier_rationale: This is the array bound for the segment index references at line 642, so a value that disagrees with the records written leaves the parser inside the sidx box and every box after it is read from the wrong offset.
mp4box.reference_count.description: The number of subsegment references that follow in this segment index.
mp4box.reference_count.algorithm: count of the str_sidx records written into the references array
mp4box.reference_count.covers: nothing in the byte stream; it is the element count of the array at line 642, each record being three 32-bit words, so 12 bytes
mp4box.reference_count.size_identity: sizeof(references) == 12 * reference_count; the sidx box size must equal 12 + 8 + (version == 0 ? 8 : 16) + 4 + 12 * reference_count
mp4box.reference_count.notes: Tier A as an identity; how many subsegments to index is free and is a real diversity axis, since a one-reference index and a many-reference index drive different paths through a client's seek table.

mp4box.default_sample_description_index.tier_rationale: The fallback stsd index for fragments of this track; an out-of-range value makes a reader fall back further rather than refuse the file, and that fallback is the branch a valid index never reaches.
mp4box.default_sample_description_index.description: Which stsd sample entry applies to fragments of this track by default, counted from 1.

mp4box.fragment_duration.tier_rationale: The total duration a fragmented file declares up front; a reader uses it to report length and never refuses a file over it, and pinning it would make every fragmented file claim the same duration.
mp4box.fragment_duration.description: Total duration of the fragmented movie in movie timescale units, 32-bit at version 0 and 64-bit at version 1.
mp4box.fragment_duration.notes: Zero, meaning unknown, is meaningful for live streams and must stay reachable; a duration that disagrees with the fragments actually present is accepted and reaches a reader's duration-correction path.

mp4box.entries.tier_rationale: The stsd sample entries are the hardest measured gate in this format: a sample entry whose declared size is 0, or whose size truncates the codec configuration box out of it, makes ffmpeg report 'invalid size 0 in stsd' and create NO STREAM AT ALL, so nothing is demuxed and no decoder is ever instantiated.
mp4box.entries.description: The sample description entries of a stsd box, each a complete box whose four-character type names a codec and whose body is the codec's sample entry and configuration; also the name of the elst edit list array at line 719.
mp4box.entries.applies_when: stsd at line 667, where this specification applies; and elst at line 719, where the array is elst_entry records whose constraints live under the elst_entry struct and which carry no payload requirement
mp4box.entries.codec: ISO/IEC 14496-12 SampleEntry, plus the codec configuration box it contains -- AVCDecoderConfigurationRecord (ISO/IEC 14496-15) for avc1, AudioSpecificConfig inside an esds for mp4a
mp4box.entries.must_produce: Each entry is a box: a uint32 size, a four-character format code, then 6 reserved bytes that must be zero and a uint16 data_reference_index that must be at least 1. For a VisualSampleEntry such as avc1 the body continues with uint16 pre_defined, uint16 reserved, uint32 pre_defined[3], uint16 width, uint16 height, uint32 horizresolution, uint32 vertresolution, uint32 reserved, uint16 frame_count, a 32-byte counted compressorname, uint16 depth and int16 pre_defined, making the entry 86 bytes before any nested box. For an AudioSampleEntry such as mp4a the body continues with uint32 reserved[2], uint16 channelcount, uint16 samplesize, uint16 pre_defined, uint16 reserved and a 16.16 samplerate, making it 36 bytes. A codec configuration box must then be nested inside the entry and inside its declared size: for avc1 an avcC holding configurationVersion 1, the three profile and level bytes, a byte whose low two bits are lengthSizeMinusOne and whose upper bits are set, a byte whose low five bits are the SPS count, then each SPS as a uint16 length and that many bytes, then the PPS count and each PPS the same way.
mp4box.entries.decoder_gate: MEASURED on a working hand-built file, by corrupting one thing at a time and running ffprobe: declaring the sample entry's size as 0 gives 'invalid size 0 in stsd' and NO STREAM AT ALL; declaring it as 8, 16, 40, 78 or 86 -- any size that leaves the avcC outside the entry -- also gives NO STREAM AT ALL; setting the stsd entry_count to 5 with one entry present gives 'invalid size 5 in stsd' and NO STREAM. Weaker failures still cost every frame: randomising the avcC body leaves the stream listed but the h264 decoder reports 'No start code is found' and decodes nothing, and corrupting the six reserved bytes shifts the width and height reads so ffmpeg reports 'Picture size 0x0' and produces no frames. Removing the stsd box entirely leaves the codec 'unknown' with zero frames.
mp4box.entries.generation_strategy: Write the entry as a box and fill its size in last. Body: 6 zero bytes, then uint16 1 for data_reference_index. For avc1 continue with uint16 0, uint16 0, three uint32 zeros, then uint16 width and uint16 height taken FROM THE TRACK'S DECLARED GEOMETRY -- these were measured to be free, since ffprobe reports the geometry from the SPS and decoded correctly with 1, 7, 64 and 1920 written here -- then uint32 0x00480000 twice for the 72 dpi resolutions, uint32 0, uint16 1 for frame_count, one length byte followed by 31 bytes for the compressorname, uint16 0x0018 for depth and int16 -1. Then nest an avcC box: size, 'avcC', then 0x01, one profile byte, one compatibility byte, one level byte, then 0xFF for lengthSizeMinusOne 3, then 0xE1 for one SPS, then a uint16 SPS length and the SPS bytes, then 0x01 and a uint16 PPS length and the PPS bytes. A verified working pair is SPS 6742c00adc47b0110000030001000003000a0f122780 (22 bytes) and PPS 68ce0f2c80 (5 bytes), giving a 38-byte avcC. Finally set the entry's size to everything written and the stsd entry_count to the number of entries. This exact construction was built and ffmpeg decoded every frame from it with no error.
mp4box.entries.measured_gate: see decoder_gate; the four NO-STREAM cases are the only ones found anywhere in this format that stop stream creation outright
mp4box.entries.notes: content_is_free is true in the important sense: the width and height written here, the compressorname, the profile and level bytes and the SPS and PPS payloads are all free and should vary, while only the framing -- the entry's size, the six reserved bytes, the data_reference_index and the nesting of the configuration box inside the declared size -- is fixed. That is the whole depth-and-diversity trade for MP4. Note in particular that the declared width and height are NOT the real geometry for H.264: the SPS overrides them, which was confirmed by writing 1920x1080 into a 64x48 stream and watching ffprobe still report 64x48 and decode correctly. They must therefore stay completely free.

mp4box.data.tier_rationale: A fixed twenty-byte run the template reads from an enca box without inspecting it; nothing validates its contents, so constraining them would remove variation and reach nothing.
mp4box.data.description: The fixed 20-byte body the template reads from an encrypted-audio sample entry.
mp4box.data.notes: Asked the question the checklist requires: an enca box is really an AudioSampleEntry, so these twenty bytes are the reserved words, channel count, sample size, pre-defined and sample rate of that entry, followed in a real file by a sinf box that the template's fixed length does not account for. The template's 20-byte read at line 673 is shorter than the 28-byte audio sample entry body the format defines, so this branch misparses any real enca box; that is a template limitation rather than a format rule, and a generator targeting a real reader should build enca through the sample-entry construction on mp4box.entries instead.

mp4box.chunk_offset.tier_rationale: These are absolute file offsets at which a reader expects to find the media bytes; MEASURED, moving a working file's single chunk offset by 100 bytes left ffmpeg listing the h264 stream but reporting 'Invalid NAL unit size (539828328 > 1323)' and decoding zero frames, so every sample is lost.
mp4box.chunk_offset.description: The array of absolute file offsets at which each chunk of media data begins, 32-bit in stco and 64-bit in co64.
mp4box.chunk_offset.algorithm: absolute byte offset from the start of the file to the first byte of each chunk; chunk n begins where chunk n-1 ended, given the sample sizes stsz declares and the samples-per-chunk stsc declares
mp4box.chunk_offset.covers: nothing in the byte stream; each element points into the mdat box at the chunk it locates
mp4box.chunk_offset.applies_when: stco at line 691 with 32-bit offsets, and co64 at line 697 with 64-bit offsets
mp4box.chunk_offset.size_identity: the array holds entry_count elements of 4 bytes in stco or 8 bytes in co64; the first offset equals the file position of the first media byte inside mdat, which in the verified construction was len(ftyp) + len(moov) + 8
mp4box.chunk_offset.measured_gate: MEASURED: a correct offset decoded every frame; an offset 100 bytes past the true start produced 'Invalid NAL unit size' and zero frames while the stream was still created.
mp4box.chunk_offset.notes: This is the field that couples the sample tables to the media bytes, and it is why the moov must be sized before the offsets can be written: compute the whole layout, then fill these in. Both widths must be generated -- co64 is the only route into a reader's 64-bit offset handling, and emitting it on a small file is legal and was the approach used to reach that path in the verified build.

mp4box.entry_size.tier_rationale: Each element is the byte length of one sample, and a reader steps through the media with them; MEASURED, zeroing every element of a working file's stsz table left ffmpeg listing the stream but reading zero frames, so all of the decode path is lost.
mp4box.entry_size.description: The per-sample byte sizes, present only when the stsz box's constant sample_size is zero.
mp4box.entry_size.algorithm: byte count of each sample as actually written into the mdat box, in sample order
mp4box.entry_size.covers: nothing in the byte stream; each element measures one sample inside mdat
mp4box.entry_size.size_identity: the array holds sample_count elements of 4 bytes and exists only when sample_size is 0, which the template tests at line 704; the sizes must sum to the total media bytes the chunk offsets and samples-per-chunk together span
mp4box.entry_size.measured_gate: MEASURED: all-zero sizes produced a stream with zero frames.
mp4box.entry_size.notes: Tier A as an identity, not as a pinned number: how long each sample is, and therefore how uneven the sizes are, is entirely the generator's choice and is a real diversity axis -- equal-sized samples and wildly varying ones drive different paths through a reader's buffer management. Write the samples first, then record their lengths here.

mp4box.sample_number.tier_rationale: The sync sample table lists which samples are keyframes; an out-of-range or unsorted number makes a reader build a degraded seek index rather than refuse the file, and pinning the list would delete both the no-keyframe and the all-keyframe seek paths.
mp4box.sample_number.description: The one-based numbers of the samples that are sync samples, in increasing order.
mp4box.sample_number.notes: The spec expects strictly increasing numbers within the track's sample count, but nothing enforces it and a reader given duplicates, zeros or out-of-range numbers takes its index-sanitising path. Note that the ABSENCE of a stss box means every sample is a sync sample, which is a distinct and common configuration; a generator should produce files with and without it.

mp4box.num_entries.tier_rationale: This is the array bound for the edit list entries at line 719, so a value that disagrees with the records written leaves the parser inside the elst box and every box after it is read at the wrong offset.
mp4box.num_entries.description: The number of edit list entries that follow.
mp4box.num_entries.algorithm: count of the elst_entry records written into the entries array
mp4box.num_entries.covers: nothing in the byte stream; it is the element count of the array at line 719, each record being three 32-bit words, so 12 bytes
mp4box.num_entries.size_identity: sizeof(entries) == 12 * num_entries; the elst box size must equal 12 + 4 + 12 * num_entries at version 0
mp4box.num_entries.notes: Spelled num_entries here rather than entry_count, so it is a separate key from mp4box.entry_count even though it does the same job. Tier A as an identity; how many edits to write is free, and zero, one and several edits take different paths through ffmpeg's edit-list handling -- a single edit with media_time 0 is the trivial case, while several edits or an empty edit reach the presentation-delay and gap-insertion code.

mp4box.major_brand.tier_rationale: MEASURED: removing the entire ftyp box from a working file left ffmpeg demuxing and listing the stream unchanged, so the brand is not a front gate for a real reader at all; but it is a registered enumeration and a reader that honours it switches on which specification the file claims to follow.
mp4box.major_brand.description: The four-character brand naming the specification this file best conforms to, the first field of the ftyp box.
mp4box.major_brand.completeness_reason: Brands are registered continuously and the field is four free bytes, so the list cannot be closed; unregistered brands are legal, are ignored, and reach a reader's unknown-brand path, which must also be generated.
mp4box.major_brand.notes: The template header at line 10 names 'ftyp' at offset 4 as this format's closest equivalent of a magic number, and a file-type probe scores a file much higher when it is present -- but ffmpeg's demuxer does not require it, which was measured. 'qt  ' and 'M4A ' carry trailing spaces that are part of the four bytes. The brand is where a reader decides whether to expect QuickTime or ISO layouts, so varying it is worth real coverage.

mp4box.minor_version.tier_rationale: An informational version number that readers store and ignore; no value makes a reader refuse the file, so pinning it would remove the only free field the ftyp box has.
mp4box.minor_version.description: The minor version of the major brand, conventionally a packed date or a small integer.
mp4box.minor_version.notes: Real files carry 0, 1, 0x200 and packed dates such as 0x20040000 here; none is privileged and all parse identically.

mp4box.type.tier_rationale: The handler component type is stored and, in ISO files, expected to be zero; a reader that does not recognise it still parses the track rather than refusing the file, so it is not a front gate, but the QuickTime values it can take select different handler interpretations.
mp4box.type.description: The hdlr box's component type; zero in ISO files, or a QuickTime component class such as a media or data handler.
mp4box.type.notes: ISO/IEC 14496-12 calls this field pre_defined and requires four zero bytes; QuickTime puts a component type here instead, and the template's name follows QuickTime. Both forms are legal in the wild and a reader handles both, so both should be generated -- the all-zero form is what every ISO writer produces and 'mhlr' is what QuickTime writers produce.

mp4box.subtype.tier_rationale: This is the handler type that tells a reader what kind of media the track carries, and a reader that does not recognise it creates the track as data rather than refusing the file; it is a registered enumeration in which each value routes the track to a different media-specific header and sample-entry parser.
mp4box.subtype.description: The hdlr box's handler type, naming the media kind of this track.
mp4box.subtype.completeness_reason: The handler registry is open-ended and the field is four free bytes; the values above are the ones real readers branch on. Unregistered handler types are legal and reach the generic-track path, which must also be generated.
mp4box.subtype.notes: This is the single most branch-rich enumeration in the format after the box type itself: 'vide' makes a reader expect a vmhd and a visual sample entry, 'soun' an smhd and an audio sample entry, 'hint' a hmhd, and 'meta', 'text' and 'subt' each their own header and entry shape. A corpus fixed at 'vide' leaves every audio, subtitle and metadata parser unreached. The template models only vmhd and smhd, so the others fall to the skip path in the template while a real reader parses them fully.

mp4box.mfr.tier_rationale: The QuickTime component manufacturer, which ISO files leave as reserved zero and which no reader inspects; per the rule for reserved fields nobody checks it stays free.
mp4box.mfr.description: The hdlr box's component manufacturer, the first of the three reserved words in the ISO layout.

mp4box.flags_mask.tier_rationale: The QuickTime component flags mask, reserved and zero in ISO files and inspected by nothing; it stays free.
mp4box.flags_mask.description: The hdlr box's component flags mask, the second of the three reserved words in the ISO layout.
mp4box.flags_mask.notes: The template reads only two of the three reserved words by name -- mfr and flags_mask -- and sweeps the third into mp4box.rest along with the handler name.

mp4box.rest.tier_rationale: Everything left in the hdlr box after the fields the template names, which is the third reserved word and the human-readable handler name; readers either skip it or copy it into metadata, and no value makes one refuse the file.
mp4box.rest.description: The remainder of the hdlr box: one more reserved word followed by the handler's name.
mp4box.rest.size_identity: sizeof(rest) == contentsize - (FTell() - startof(version)), which after the fields the template names is contentsize - 24
mp4box.rest.notes: Asked the question the checklist requires: the format says the tail is a name string, but the two conventions disagree -- ISO uses a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string filling the box, QuickTime a Pascal-style counted string whose first byte is the length. The template's own comment at lines 736-737 says exactly this and declines to model it. Both conventions parse as free bytes here, both are produced by real writers, and a reader that displays the name takes a different path for each, so both are worth generating and neither is constrained.

mp4box.time_scale.tier_rationale: The number of time units per second, in the movie header or a media header; the prompt names timescales as Tier C alongside sample rates, no reader refuses any value, and pinning it would give every generated file the same time base.
mp4box.time_scale.description: Number of time units that pass per second, against which this box's durations are expressed.

evidence.snippet: uint32 time_scale <name="Time Scale", comment="Number of media time units per second">;

mp4box.time_scale.applies_when: mdhd at line 745, where it is the media timescale, and mvhd at line 755, where it is the movie timescale

cross_check.snippet: uint32 time_scale <name="Time Scale", comment="Number of movie time units per second">;

mp4box.time_scale.measured_gate: MEASURED: the verified hand-built file decoded correctly with timescales of 1, 5, 1000 and 90000, so this field is genuinely free and was confirmed not to gate anything.
mp4box.time_scale.notes: Zero is deliberately not excluded: it is the value that makes every duration-to-seconds conversion divide by zero and is the only way to reach those guards. The movie and media timescales need not agree with each other and a reader rescales between them, so writing different values in mvhd and mdhd is worthwhile and exercises the rescaling arithmetic.

mp4box.duration.tier_rationale: A duration in timescale units, declared in the movie header, the media header and the track header; a reader reports it and corrects it against the sample tables rather than refusing the file, and pinning it would make every file claim the same length.
mp4box.duration.description: Length of the movie, media or track, expressed in the relevant timescale.

evidence.snippet: uint32 duration <name="Duration", comment="Duration of the media in media time scale units">;

mp4box.duration.applies_when: mdhd at line 746 in media timescale units, mvhd at line 756 in movie timescale units, and tkhd at line 782 in movie timescale units

per_box_semantics.mdhd: the track's media duration in its own media timescale
per_box_semantics.mvhd: the longest track's duration in the movie timescale
per_box_semantics.tkhd: this track's duration in the movie timescale, after the edit list is applied

cross_check.snippet: uint32 duration <name="Duration", comment="Duration of the media in movie time scale units (specified in mvhd box)">;

mp4box.duration.notes: The all-ones value 0xFFFFFFFF is the spec's sentinel for an unknown duration, used by live and fragmented files, and is the single most interesting value this field can take -- it drives a reader down its indeterminate-length path. A duration that disagrees with what the sample tables imply is accepted and reaches the duration-correction code. Nothing is excluded.

mp4box.quality.tier_rationale: The media header's quality field, which the spec reserves and no reader inspects; it stays free.
mp4box.quality.description: The mdhd box's quality field, reserved in ISO files and a playback quality hint in QuickTime.

mp4box.flags.tier_rationale: Declared five times as an uninspected three-byte flags word -- in elst, hdlr, mdhd, mvhd and smhd, none of which defines any flag -- and twice more as a structured flags value whose bits carry their own entries under tkhd_flags and vmhd_flags; in the five uninspected cases nothing validates the bytes, so they stay free.
mp4box.flags.description: The 24-bit flags word of a full box that defines no flags, or, at lines 777 and 794, the structured track-header and video-media-header flags.
mp4box.flags.applies_when: elst (717), hdlr (731), mdhd (742), mvhd (752) and smhd (771) as an uninspected byte[3]; tkhd (777) as a tkhd_flags whose four bits are constrained under that struct; vmhd (794) as a vmhd_flags whose single defined bit is constrained under that struct
mp4box.flags.notes: Spelled flags here and flag at the twenty other sites, so the two are separate keys even though they are the same concept; mp4box.flag carries the presence bitmask for trun, tfhd, saio, saiz and senc. For smhd the spec actually requires the flags word to be 1, as it does for vmhd, but nothing validates it and ffmpeg ignores it, so it is left free here.

mp4box.preview_time.tier_rationale: A QuickTime preview start time that ISO readers treat as reserved and ignore; no value makes a reader refuse the file, so pinning it removes variation for nothing.
mp4box.preview_time.description: Time in the movie at which the preview begins, in movie timescale units.

evidence.snippet: uint32 preview_time <name="Preview Time", comment="Time value in the movie at which the preview begins">;

mp4box.preview_time.notes: This and the five fields that follow it occupy the twenty-four bytes ISO/IEC 14496-12 calls pre_defined[6] and requires to be zero; QuickTime gives them the meanings the template uses. Non-zero values are legal QuickTime and ignored ISO, so they stay free.

mp4box.preview_duration.tier_rationale: A QuickTime preview length, reserved and ignored by ISO readers; free.
mp4box.preview_duration.description: Duration of the movie preview in movie timescale units.

evidence.snippet: uint32 preview_duration <name="Preview Duration", comment="Duration of the movie preview in movie time scale units">;

mp4box.poster_time.tier_rationale: A QuickTime poster frame time, reserved and ignored by ISO readers; free.
mp4box.poster_time.description: Time in the movie of the poster frame, in movie timescale units.

evidence.snippet: uint32 poster_time <name="Poster Time", comment="Time value in the movie of the movie poster">;

mp4box.selection_time.tier_rationale: A QuickTime selection start, reserved and ignored by ISO readers; free.
mp4box.selection_time.description: Start time of the current selection in movie timescale units.

evidence.snippet: uint32 selection_time <name="Selection Time", comment="Start time of the current selection">;

mp4box.selection_duration.tier_rationale: A QuickTime selection length, reserved and ignored by ISO readers; free.
mp4box.selection_duration.description: Duration of the current selection in movie timescale units.

evidence.snippet: uint32 selection_duration <name="Selection Duration", comment="Duration of the current selection in movie time scale units">;

mp4box.current_time.tier_rationale: A QuickTime playhead position, reserved and ignored by ISO readers; free.
mp4box.current_time.description: Current time position within the movie, in movie timescale units.

evidence.snippet: uint32 current_time <name="Current Time", comment="Time value of current time position within the movie">;

mp4box.next_track_id.tier_rationale: A hint to a writer about which track identifier to allocate next; readers store it and never validate it, so pinning it would remove variation without touching a branch.
mp4box.next_track_id.description: The track identifier a writer should use for the next track it adds.

evidence.snippet: uint32 next_track_id <name="Next Track ID", comment="The value to use for the track ID number of the next track added">;

mp4box.next_track_id.notes: The all-ones value 0xFFFFFFFF is the spec's marker that every identifier is taken and a writer must search for a free one; it is legal, meaningful and worth emitting. A value that collides with an existing track_id is also accepted.

mp4box.track_id.tier_rationale: The track's own identifier, which fragments and track-extends boxes reference by value; a duplicate or zero identifier makes a reader report a conflict rather than refuse the file, and pinning it to 1 would leave every multi-track and dangling-reference path unreached.
mp4box.track_id.description: The unique identifier of this track within the movie.
mp4box.track_id.notes: The spec reserves 0 as meaning no track and requires identifiers to be unique and below the mvhd next_track_id; none of that is enforced, and zero, duplicates and out-of-range identifiers all reach a reader's conflict handling. The matching rule against tfhd and trex trackID is recorded as a dependency rather than pinned here.

mp4box.reserved3.tier_rationale: The track header's reserved half-word after the volume, which the spec requires to be zero and which no reader inspects; per the rule for reserved fields nobody checks, it stays free.
mp4box.reserved3.description: The reserved 16-bit field between the track volume and the matrix.

mp4box.layer.tier_rationale: The front-to-back ordering of this track against others, which a compositor sorts by; no value makes a reader refuse the file, and pinning it to zero would leave every layered composition path unreached.
mp4box.layer.description: The track's composition layer; lower values are nearer the viewer and the field is signed in the specification.
mp4box.layer.notes: The template declares this unsigned but the spec defines it signed, so values at or above 0x8000 are negative layers -- in front of everything -- which is legal and reaches a compositor's ordering code that non-negative values never do.

mp4box.alt_group.tier_rationale: The alternate group this track belongs to, from which a player picks exactly one track; a reader groups tracks by the value and never refuses a file over it, and pinning it to zero would leave the whole track-selection path unreached.
mp4box.alt_group.description: The alternate group identifier; tracks sharing a non-zero value are alternatives to one another and a player selects one.
mp4box.alt_group.notes: Zero means the track belongs to no alternate group and is always played, which is the common case; a non-zero value shared by two tracks is what triggers a player's language or bitrate selection logic, so both must be generated.

mp4box.width.tier_rationale: MEASURED: the verified hand-built file decoded correctly with this field declaring 1, 7, 64 and 1920, and ffprobe reported the real geometry from the codec's own parameter set regardless, so the field is genuinely free -- and it is exactly the dimension a size-conscious author is tempted to pin, which is the mistake this extraction exists to avoid.
mp4box.width.description: The track's display width as a 16.16 fixed-point value in the track header.
mp4box.width.measured_gate: MEASURED: declaring 1920x1080 on a stream whose SPS says 64x48 left ffprobe reporting 64x48 and decoding every frame without error; the container dimensions are presentation metadata, not decode parameters, for any codec that carries its own geometry.
mp4box.width.notes: DO NOT NARROW THIS FIELD. It is a 16.16 fixed-point value, so the pixel width is the high sixteen bits and the low sixteen are a fraction; non-integer widths are legal and reach a player's scaling arithmetic. Zero is meaningful -- a track with zero width is non-visual -- and must stay reachable. The width interacts with the matrix and with the sample entry's own width, and a mismatch between the three is accepted by readers and drives their aspect-ratio reconciliation code, so they should be allowed to disagree rather than being locked together. File size is bounded by the output_budget on the box sequence, never by this field.

mp4box.height.tier_rationale: As with the width, this was measured to be free -- the codec's parameter set overrides it and the file still decoded at every value tried -- and it is the second half of the dimension pair a careful reader is most tempted to pin.
mp4box.height.description: The track's display height as a 16.16 fixed-point value in the track header.
mp4box.height.measured_gate: MEASURED alongside mp4box.width; declared heights of 1, 13, 48 and 1080 all decoded identically.
mp4box.height.notes: DO NOT NARROW THIS FIELD. Zero, fractional values and values far larger than any real display are all legal and accepted, and each reaches different scaling and aspect-ratio code. The displayed geometry is the track dimensions transformed by the matrix, so unusual pairs here combined with a rotation matrix are what exercise a player's presentation pipeline.

mp4box.graphics_mode.tier_rationale: A graphics mode a reader does not implement falls back on a plain copy rather than refusing the file, so it is not a front gate; but it is a closed typedef enum in this template and each mode selects a different compositing operation.
mp4box.graphics_mode.description: The QuickTime transfer mode used when compositing this video track, from the video media header.
mp4box.graphics_mode.notes: Taken verbatim from the qtgfxmode enum at lines 152-163, which declares the values in hexadecimal as 0x000, 0x040, 0x020, 0x024, 0x100, 0x101, 0x102, 0x104 and 0x103 -- note that the template lists them out of numeric order, with qtgComposition (0x103) declared last after qtgStraightAlphaBlend (0x104). Every one is preferred: qtgCopy is the plain overwrite, qtgTransparent and qtgBlend are the only modes that make the opcolor meaningful, and the four alpha modes each select a different premultiplication convention. Values outside the enum are representable and reach a reader's unknown-mode fallback, which is worth generating too, but they are not listed as legal because the enum is closed.

then.rule: the 64-bit size field is present and carries the real box length, which must be at least 16 because the header it measures is itself 16 bytes

dependencies.description: The template tests size == 1 at line 374 and only then reads size64; the two are mutually exclusive ways of expressing one length.

then.rule: the box extends to end of file, so it must be the last box at its nesting level; ffmpeg was MEASURED to handle this correctly, but the template's BoxSize helper at line 172 returns 0 and collapses endOffset onto startOffset

dependencies.description: Size 0 is legal ISO and worth generating for a real reader, but it is a template limitation rather than a format one.

then.rule: in trun the composition offset becomes a signed int32 (line 605) rather than an unsigned uint32 (line 603), which is the only way to express negative presentation reordering

dependencies.description: The version byte selects the signedness, and negative offsets are what a stream with B-frames needs.

then.rule: the saio offsets become 64-bit (line 569) rather than 32-bit (line 567); the same version split governs sidx earliest_presentation_time and first_offset at lines 630-639 and mehd fragment_duration at lines 656-659

dependencies.description: Version 1 of these boxes exists purely to widen their offset and time fields, so it is the only route into every 64-bit path in the format.

then.rule: a pssh box of version 1 or later carries a key identifier count and that many 16-byte identifiers before DataSize; at version 0 neither field exists

dependencies.description: The template tests version > 0 at line 528 and only then reads the key identifier list, so the version changes the box's layout entirely.

then.rule: a tenc box of version 0 has a second reserved byte at line 506; any other version replaces it with default_crypt_skip_byte_block at line 507, which is where the pattern encryption parameters live

dependencies.description: The version byte swaps one byte's meaning entirely, so pattern encryption is unreachable at version 0.

then.rule: a constant IV size and that many IV bytes are present; when the per-sample IV size is non-zero neither field exists and the IV travels per sample in the senc box instead

dependencies.description: The template tests this at line 511; it is the branch that decides whether initialisation vectors are constant or per-sample, and the two are structurally different files.

then.rule: in a senc box the subsample count and its table are present; the template tests flag[2] == 2 at line 546 with an equality rather than a bit test, so a senc whose flags are 0x000003 would have its subsamples skipped by this template even though a reader parses them

dependencies.description: Partial-sample encryption is the common case for video, and this is the flag that brings the clear-and-protected range table into existence.

then.rule: the stsz box carries a per-sample size table of sample_count 32-bit entries; when sample_size is non-zero the table is absent and every sample shares that one size

dependencies.description: The template tests this at line 704; the sentinel 0 is what turns a fixed-length box into a variable-length one.

then.rule: the saiz box carries a per-sample size byte for each of sample_count samples; when the default is non-zero the table is absent

dependencies.description: The template tests this at line 581, mirroring the stsz sentinel.

ISO/IEC 14496-12 requires a video track's minf to contain a video media header; a reader that finds the wrong header for the handler type reports an inconsistency rather than refusing the file, so the mismatch is worth generating too.
An audio track's minf must contain a sound media header, and the sample entries in its stsd must be AudioSampleEntry rather than VisualSampleEntry shaped.

then.rule: the stsd entries must use the 86-byte VisualSampleEntry layout with width, height, resolutions, frame_count, compressorname and depth before any nested configuration box

dependencies.description: The handler type decides which of the two sample entry shapes the stsd entries take, and the shapes differ in length by fifty bytes; getting it wrong was MEASURED to cost the stream entirely.

then.rule: the stsd entries must use the 36-byte AudioSampleEntry layout with channelcount, samplesize and a 16.16 samplerate before any nested configuration box

dependencies.description: The audio sample entry is shorter than the visual one and carries different fields in the same positions.

then.rule: the number of sample entry boxes physically present must equal entry_count exactly, and their sizes must sum to the stsd box size minus 16; MEASURED, a disagreement gives 'invalid size N in stsd' and no stream at all

dependencies.description: This is the hardest gate measured anywhere in the format, and it is a count-versus-content agreement rather than a value constraint.

then.rule: for the reference to resolve the index should be between 1 and the stsd entry_count; out-of-range values are accepted and reach a reader's fallback to the first description

dependencies.description: A cross-box index whose conforming span follows another box's count, which is a real format rule rather than an arbitrary narrowing; both the resolving and the dangling case are wanted.

then.rule: a tfhd or trex trackID should match some track's tkhd track_id for the fragment to apply; a dangling identifier makes a reader skip the fragment, which is its own branch

dependencies.description: The fragment-to-track binding is by value, and both the matching and the dangling case are worth generating.

ISO/IEC 14496-12 requires a movie extends box inside moov whenever movie fragments follow, so a reader knows to expect them; ffmpeg tolerates its absence and still parses the fragments, which is a separate recovery path.
A sample table carries either 32-bit or 64-bit chunk offsets, never both; they are two encodings of the same table and a reader that meets both uses whichever it read last.

then.rule: each offset must be the absolute file position of that chunk's first media byte, which depends on the final sizes of ftyp, moov and every box before mdat; MEASURED, an offset 100 bytes off gave 'Invalid NAL unit size' and zero frames

dependencies.description: The sample tables and the media bytes are coupled only through these offsets, which is why the whole file layout must be settled before they can be written.

then.rule: the stsz entry_size array holds exactly sample_count elements, and those sizes must sum to the media bytes the chunk offsets and str_stsc.samples_per_chunk together span

dependencies.description: The three sample-table boxes describe one set of bytes from three directions and must agree; ffmpeg builds its index from all three at once.

then.rule: the first stsc entry must have first_chunk equal to 1, each later entry must be strictly greater than the one before, and none may exceed the chunk count the stco or co64 box declares

dependencies.description: The sample-to-chunk table is run-length coded and a reader walks it assuming monotonic boundaries; breaking that gives an empty or wrong sample index.

then.rule: the senc per-sample IV should be default_per_sample_IV_size bytes wide, but the template hard-codes it at 8 bytes at line 545, so a file using 16-byte IVs is misparsed by this template although readers handle it

dependencies.description: A template limitation rather than a format rule, recorded so the generator knows the two disagree.

then.rule: with no mdat box there are no media bytes to point at, so a track's sample tables should declare zero samples; a non-empty table pointing outside any box makes a reader read garbage and decode nothing

dependencies.description: A moov-only file is legal and parses, and it is the configuration a reader reports as having no frames, which is a distinct and reachable state.
The graphics mode lives in the vmhd box, which only a video track has, so the enumeration applies only when the handler type is vide.

structure.subject: the ftyp box
structure.detail: a conforming file begins with a file type box naming its major brand and compatible brands
structure.description: ISO/IEC 14496-12 requires ftyp first and the template's own header at line 10 names it as this format's identifying bytes; MEASURED, however, ffmpeg demuxed a working file unchanged with the whole ftyp box removed, so it is a probe aid rather than a hard gate.
structure.generation_note: emit as a fixed head box: size, 'ftyp', the major brand, the minor version, then one or more compatible brands filling the declared size

structure.subject: the moov box
structure.detail: exactly one movie box, containing one mvhd and at least one trak
structure.description: Without moov a reader has no track descriptions and reports that no streams were found; this is the box the whole format exists to carry.
structure.output_budget: 262144 bytes (256 KiB) for the entire moov subtree, tracked as a running total the generator checks before adding each track or table entry. The sample tables are the variable part and grow with the sample count, so the generator stops adding samples when this is reached rather than shrinking any field.
structure.generation_note: build the subtree depth first so every container's size can be filled in from its children, then compute the chunk offsets last because they depend on moov's final size

structure.subject: the track subtree moov > trak > mdia > minf > stbl
structure.detail: a decodable track requires the full chain, with stbl containing at minimum a stsd, and in practice also stts, stsc, stsz and stco or co64
structure.description: MEASURED: removing the stsd box left ffmpeg reporting the codec as 'unknown' with zero frames, and setting stts entry_count to 0 gave 'stream 0, missing mandatory atoms'; the chain is what turns a parsed container into a decodable stream.
structure.output_budget: covered by the 256 KiB moov budget; each sample costs 4 bytes in stsz and each chunk 4 or 8 bytes in stco, which the running total should count
structure.generation_note: emit the five containers as nested boxes in that order, then the sample table boxes inside stbl; the thirteen container types the template walks are listed at lines 472-484 and only those have their bodies parsed as further boxes

structure.subject: the stsd box and its sample entries
structure.detail: stsd must contain exactly entry_count sample entry boxes whose sizes sum to the stsd box size minus 16, and each entry must contain its codec configuration box within its own declared size
structure.description: This is the only measured gate in the format that stops stream creation outright, so it is the single highest-value structure to get right.
structure.output_budget: 16384 bytes across all stsd boxes in the file; a sample entry with an avcC is roughly 132 bytes, so this allows many tracks and many entries per track while the entry count itself stays free
structure.generation_note: write each entry as a box with its size filled in last, nest the configuration box inside it, then set entry_count from the number of entries actually written

structure.subject: the mdat box
structure.detail: the media bytes live in one or more media data boxes that the sample tables address by absolute file offset; mdat is absent from the template's switch and is consumed by FSkip at line 799
structure.description: A file with sample tables but no mdat parses and reports a stream with no readable frames, which is itself a reachable state worth generating occasionally.
structure.output_budget: 786432 bytes (768 KiB) of media data summed across every mdat box, counted as body bytes. The generator keeps a running total and stops adding samples once it is reached. It never shrinks a declared dimension, a timescale or a sample count to save space -- the budget is spent by ending the sample sequence.
structure.generation_note: emit after moov so the chunk offsets can be computed from moov's final size, or before it with a two-pass layout; either order is legal and readers handle both, and mdat-first is what streaming writers produce

structure.subject: the moov and mdat boxes
structure.detail: either may come first; moov before mdat is the progressive-download layout and mdat before moov is what a recorder writes as it goes
structure.description: Both orders are legal and common, and a reader takes a different path for each -- with moov last it must seek to the end before it can index anything.
structure.output_budget: covered by the moov and mdat budgets; the ordering costs no extra bytes
structure.generation_note: generate both orders; the chunk offsets are absolute, so whichever order is chosen the offsets must be computed after both box sizes are known

structure.subject: the top-level box sequence
structure.detail: boxes repeat until end of file, each an 8-byte or 16-byte header followed by its body; the template's main loop at line 804 runs while FTell() is below FileSize()
structure.description: The box count and the mix of types are the file's principal repeating dimensions, and unknown types are skipped rather than refused.
structure.output_budget: 1048576 bytes (1 MiB) for the whole file, tracked as a running total the generator checks before starting each top-level box; the sub-allocations above -- 768 KiB of media data, 256 KiB of moov, 16 KiB of sample descriptions -- are parts of this figure. A megabyte holds a multi-track movie with real sample tables and a fragment or two while keeping generation and decoding fast across a large corpus. NO FIELD IS NARROWED TO ACHIEVE THIS: the track dimensions, timescales, durations and sample counts all stay free and the budget is spent by ending the box sequence.
structure.generation_note: emit as a fixed head (ftyp), then the moov subtree and the mdat, then any further top-level boxes bounded by the running total; there is no trailer, since the loop simply ends at end of file

structure.subject: free, skip and unregistered top-level boxes
structure.detail: any number, anywhere, each skipped by size
structure.description: The default arm of the switch at line 798 skips them and so does every reader, which makes them the only route into the unknown-box path.
structure.output_budget: 65536 bytes (64 KiB) across every free, skip and unregistered box, tracked as a running total; the number of such boxes and each one's size stay free within it
structure.generation_note: scatter them between the known boxes rather than clustering them, and mix registered-but-unmodelled types with wholly invented four-character codes, since a reader has handlers for the first group and only a skip for the second

structure.subject: the moof box
structure.detail: a movie fragment contains an mfhd and one or more traf, each traf containing a tfhd and zero or more trun
structure.description: The fragment subtree is a second, parallel way of describing samples, and it reaches a completely different body of reader code from the sample tables in moov.
structure.output_budget: 131072 bytes (128 KiB) across every moof subtree in the file, tracked as a running total; how many fragments to emit and how many runs each carries stay free within it
structure.generation_note: emit moof and its following mdat as a repeated pair after the moov, incrementing mfhd sequence_number across fragments; vary which tfhd and trun flag bits are set, because those bits decide which optional fields exist and are a major diversity axis

structure.subject: the stco and co64 boxes
structure.detail: a sample table carries one or the other, never both
structure.description: They are two encodings of the same chunk offset table, differing only in offset width.
structure.output_budget: covered by the moov budget at 4 or 8 bytes per chunk
structure.generation_note: choose between them freely rather than always using stco; co64 is the only route into a reader's 64-bit offset handling and is legal on a small file

structure.subject: the mvhd box
structure.detail: the movie header must be the first box inside moov, before any trak
structure.description: Readers expect the movie timescale to be known before they parse tracks that express durations in it.
structure.generation_note: emit mvhd first inside moov, then one trak per track

structure.subject: the trak box
structure.detail: one or more, each describing a single track
structure.description: A multi-track file exercises a reader's stream selection, alternate groups and interleaving, none of which a single-track corpus reaches.
structure.output_budget: covered by the 256 KiB moov budget; each track costs roughly 500 bytes of headers plus its sample tables, so the track count stays free within that total
structure.generation_note: emit several tracks with different handler subtypes -- vide, soun, text, meta -- rather than only video, since the handler type selects which media header and sample entry shape a reader parses

structure.subject: the dinf and dref boxes
structure.detail: a conforming minf contains a data information box holding a data reference box with at least one entry, conventionally a self-contained 'url ' with its flags set to 1
structure.description: The sample entries' data_reference_index points into this table, so an entry index of 1 with no dref present is a dangling reference that readers tolerate but conformance checkers flag.
structure.output_budget: covered by the moov budget at 36 bytes for the usual single self-contained entry
structure.generation_note: emit dinf > dref with one 12-byte 'url ' full box whose flags are 1, which is what the verified hand-built file used

structure.subject: boxes inside stbl
structure.detail: stsd conventionally comes first, followed by stts, then the optional stss, then stsc, stsz and finally stco or co64
structure.description: The order is conventional rather than mandatory -- readers index the boxes by type -- but the conventional order is what every writer produces and what readers are tested against.
structure.generation_note: emit in the conventional order most of the time and shuffle it occasionally, since out-of-order sample tables are legal and exercise a reader's order-independent box indexing

structure.subject: a box whose declared size is smaller than its header
structure.detail: sizes 2 through 7 are smaller than the 8-byte header and no box may declare them
structure.description: The template's contentsize computation at line 467 is unsigned, so such a size underflows to an enormous value and the parse runs away; ffmpeg was measured to recover, but nothing legitimate produces one.

structure.subject: none
structure.detail: MP4 has no trailer; the box sequence simply ends at end of file, and a box whose size field is 0 claims everything to that point
structure.description: The template's loop at line 804 ends on FileSize() with no terminator to look for, so unlike GIF or PNG there is no final marker to get right.
structure.generation_note: no tail element is needed; optionally give the final top-level box a size of 0 to exercise the extends-to-end-of-file rule, which ffmpeg was measured to handle correctly

diversity_axes.why: The track display width is the dimension a size-conscious author is most tempted to pin, and it was MEASURED to be completely free: a file declaring 1920x1080 over a stream whose parameter set says 64x48 decoded every frame correctly and ffprobe simply reported the codec's geometry. Pinning it would buy nothing and cost every scaling and aspect-ratio path.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: zero width marks a non-visual track and skips the whole presentation setup; fractional 16.16 values reach the scaling arithmetic; a width disagreeing with the sample entry's own width reaches a reader's aspect-ratio reconciliation; combined with a rotation matrix it drives the display-matrix transform.

diversity_axes.why: The second half of the dimension pair, measured free alongside the width at 1, 13, 48 and 1080; narrowing it would make every generated track the same shape for no gain in depth.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: the same scaling and reconciliation paths as the width, plus the portrait-versus-landscape branch in any player that rotates by the matrix.

diversity_axes.why: Listed with the narrower meaning the tier extension describes: the VALUE is pinned by its identity with the records present and must be derived, but HOW MANY records each table holds is entirely free and is the strongest structural diversity axis in the format. A one-entry stts is a constant frame rate and a many-entry one is variable; a one-entry stco puts everything in one chunk and a many-entry one scatters it.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: the count drives the size of every table a reader allocates and the number of iterations of its index builder; a count of 0 gives 'missing mandatory atoms' and an empty index; a count that disagrees with the entries present was MEASURED to give 'invalid size N in stsd' and no stream at all.

diversity_axes.why: Same narrower meaning: the value records a free choice. How many samples a track carries is where a corpus's duration and complexity diversity comes from, and it is bounded only by the output_budget on the box sequence, never by a cap on the field.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: zero samples gives a stream with no frames; one sample exercises the single-sample fast paths; many samples drive the index builder, the chunk walk and the buffer management repeatedly; in trun the same count produces wildly different byte lengths depending on which flag bits are set.

diversity_axes.why: Same narrower meaning: each element must equal the sample it measures, but how long each sample is, and how uneven the sizes are, is entirely free. Equal-sized samples and wildly varying ones drive different paths through a reader's buffer management.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: all-zero sizes were MEASURED to give a stream with zero frames; a size larger than the bytes present makes the reader run past the chunk; uneven sizes exercise the reallocation path that constant sizes never reach.

diversity_axes.why: Same narrower meaning: each offset must point at the real chunk, but WHERE the generator puts the media -- before or after moov, in one chunk or many -- is entirely free and is what makes the offsets differ across a corpus. Pinning the layout would leave the mdat-first and multi-chunk paths unreached.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: a correct offset decodes every frame; an offset 100 bytes off was MEASURED to give 'Invalid NAL unit size' and zero frames; many small chunks exercise the chunk walk repeatedly where one large chunk does not; co64 offsets are the only route into 64-bit offset handling.

diversity_axes.why: The sample entries are the format's one payload, and their framing is Tier A, but everything inside them -- the declared geometry, the compressorname, the profile and level bytes, the parameter set payloads, and how many entries a track declares -- is free and must vary. This axis exists to stop the rewrite step freezing one canonical sample entry and reusing it everywhere.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: the format code selects which decoder is instantiated, so avc1, mp4a, hvc1 and an unregistered code reach four different outcomes; the nested configuration box's contents are what the codec parses to set up, and varying the profile and level reaches different decoder initialisation paths.

diversity_axes.why: The box type is what decides which parsing branch runs at all; every registered type left out of the generated mix is a whole handler that never executes, and unregistered types are the only route into the skip path at line 799.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: each named type maps to its own arm of the switch at lines 469-801 and to its own handler in a real reader; the thirteen container types have their bodies walked as further boxes while everything else is parsed flat or skipped.

diversity_axes.why: The handler type decides what kind of track this is and therefore which media header and which sample entry shape a reader expects; a corpus fixed at 'vide' leaves every audio, subtitle, timecode and metadata parser unreached.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 'vide' expects a vmhd and a VisualSampleEntry; 'soun' an smhd and an AudioSampleEntry fifty bytes shorter; 'hint', 'meta', 'text', 'subt' and 'tmcd' each their own header and entry shape; an unregistered handler reaches the generic data-track path.

diversity_axes.why: One byte that switches whole fields between 32-bit and 64-bit widths in six different boxes and adds the key-identifier list to pssh; emitting only version 0 leaves every 64-bit path in the format unreached.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: version 1 is the sole route into 64-bit saio offsets, 64-bit sidx times, a 64-bit mehd duration, signed trun composition offsets and the pssh KID array; version 0 is the sole route into their 32-bit counterparts.

diversity_axes.why: Listed with the narrower meaning: the bits must agree with the fields physically written, but WHICH optional fields to write is entirely free and is one of the largest diversity axes in the format. A trun carrying all four per-sample fields and one carrying none are structurally different boxes that exercise different reader code.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: each set bit adds a field to every entry of a run, so the same sample count produces different byte lengths and different parsing loops; the tfhd bits select between three different fragment addressing modes; the saio and saiz bit adds the auxiliary type fields; the senc bit brings the whole subsample table into existence.

diversity_axes.why: The timescale is named in the Tier C list alongside sample rates, and it was MEASURED free at 1, 5, 1000 and 90000; pinning it to 1000 or 90000 would give every generated file the same time base and delete the rescaling arithmetic between movie and media timescales.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: zero reaches every divide-by-zero guard in the duration arithmetic; a movie timescale differing from the media timescale forces the rescaling path; very large timescales exercise the 64-bit timestamp arithmetic.

diversity_axes.why: A duration a careful reader is tempted to derive from the sample tables and pin; doing so would delete the sentinel and the disagreement branches, which are the only interesting things this field can do.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: the all-ones sentinel drives a reader down its indeterminate-length path for live content; a duration disagreeing with the sample tables reaches the duration-correction code; zero reports an empty movie.

diversity_axes.why: The per-sample duration, which decides the frame rate; pinning it would give every generated file a constant rate and leave the variable-frame-rate handling unreached.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: zero-duration samples force the coincident-timestamp path; a single stts run is constant rate while several runs are variable; large deltas against a small timescale produce multi-hour durations and exercise the 64-bit arithmetic.

diversity_axes.why: How samples are distributed across chunks is a count feeding the index builder's inner loop, and it is exactly the field a careful reader fixes at 1; fixing it would leave the multi-sample chunk arithmetic unexercised.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: one sample per chunk makes the chunk offset table as long as the sample table and drives the chunk walk on every sample; many samples per chunk exercises the within-chunk offset accumulation; a zero count reaches the loop guard.

diversity_axes.why: The edit list start time, whose all-ones sentinel marks an empty edit; a generator restricted to small numbers would never produce that sentinel, and it is the value that drives ffmpeg's presentation-delay insertion.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: the sentinel inserts blank presentation time and shifts every timestamp in the track; a non-zero start trims the front of the media; zero is the trivial pass-through.

diversity_axes.why: The track identifier that fragments reference by value; pinning it to 1 would leave every multi-track and dangling-reference path unreached.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: a unique identifier is the ordinary case; a duplicate reaches a reader's conflict handling; zero is the reserved no-track value; an identifier no tfhd references leaves the track unfragmented while one referenced by a dangling tfhd reaches the skip path.

diversity_axes.why: Nine closed enumeration values each selecting a different compositing operation; emitting only the plain copy would leave every blend and alpha path unreached, and two of the values are the only ones that make the opcolor meaningful.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: qtgCopy is a plain overwrite; qtgTransparent and qtgBlend consult the opcolor; the four alpha modes each select a different premultiplication convention; values outside the enum reach the unknown-mode fallback.
